detail.title: Digital Identity as an Attention Signal: Evidence from AI-Generated Avatars and Stock Returns

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no competing interests.

detail.abstract: The rapid development of generative AI has increased the use of AI-generated images on social media, but their role in financial markets remains unclear. This paper examines whether investors' use of AI-generated images as profile avatars is associated with AI-related attention and short-term stock returns. Using 7,620,274 posts from 816,945 accounts on Eastmoney Guba related to CSI 300 constituents from January 2024 to July 2025, we identify accounts that use AI-generated profile avatars with an image classifier and classify stocks into AI-supply-chain and non-AI stocks. We find that these accounts are disproportionately active in discussions of AI-supply-chain stocks. Their posting intensity relative to other accounts positively predicts next-trading-day returns for AI-supply-chain stocks, with stronger effects among longer-tenured accounts. The results indicate that account-level visual identity helps identify identity-aligned attention, a source-conditioned and topic-aligned component of social-media attention that is distinct from aggregate discussion activity and contemporaneous post content.

title: Structural Learning of Financial Dependency Networks: Integrating Chow-Liu and K2 Algorithms for Systemic Risk and Portfolio Modeling
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Structural Learning of Financial Dependency Networks: Integrating Chow-Liu and K2 Algorithms for Systemic Risk and Portfolio Modeling

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses publicly available financial and sustainability data. No human participants were involved, and therefore no ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Financial markets are complex systems where shocks propagate through hidden dependency structures. Traditional risk and portfolio models rely on correlation, which is symmetric and cannot capture directionality or causal influence. This paper proposes a unified framework that bridges descriptive network topology with causal probabilistic graphical models to learn the dependency structure of financial assets. We implement a two-stage pipeline: first, we characterize the financial network using topological metrics including degree distribution and hub identification. Second, we learn a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) using the Chow-Liu algorithm to obtain a maximum-likelihood tree skeleton, followed by refinement with a greedy K2 score search. We apply the framework in Python using networkx to simulated daily returns of JSE mining companies and macroeconomic variables from 2019-2023. Empirically, we find that the topology-informed K2 search reduces computational time by 38.2% relative to random-order K2 and recovers economically meaningful causal edges such as VIX → Mining Stocks and VIX → ESG. The results suggest that global risk factors dominate domestic asset linkages in emerging markets, with direct implications for systemic risk monitoring and minimumdependency portfolio construction. For regulators, the centrality of VIX implies that macro-prudential surveillance should prioritize external transmission channels over intra-sector contagion. For investors, the DAG structure suggests that hedging JSE mining exposure requires instruments tied to global volatility rather than pairwise diversification alone. By integrating ESG as an endogenous node, the framework provides a foundation for quantifying how sustainability disclosures respond to market stress and how they in turn affect volatility. This approach offers a transparent, computationally efficient method for modeling interdependence in data-scarce environments. Code and data are provided for replication.

title: Stewardship Communities in New York Cy Pres

detail.title: Stewardship Communities in New York Cy Pres
detail.abstract: New York State charitable law protects property, but it does not always protect the people who founded and kept a charitable mission alive. Cy pres is a centuries-old doctrine of equity that answers what happens to charitable property when a gift’s original purpose becomes impossible or impracticable. In such proceedings, the courts direct the property as near as possible to the donor’s original intent under N.Y. Est. Powers & Trusts Law § 8-1.1 (McKinney 2025). A mission-oriented institution, however, is more than a legal structure or a collection of assets. It may also carry memory, worship, sacrifice, and the shared meaning of a community. When faith and cultural heritage are left out of the legal assessment, existing cy pres practice may preserve the outside shell while the heritage that undergirds the charitable purpose is lost.

title: Beyond the Transaction: UPI, Financial Inclusion, and the Limits of Digital Access in India

detail.title: Beyond the Transaction: UPI, Financial Inclusion, and the Limits of Digital Access in India
detail.abstract: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has become the backbone of India's digital economy, processing over 23 billion transactions worth roughly Rs 30 lakh crore in a single month as of mid-2026, according to National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) data, and now accounts for a large majority of India's retail digital payment volume. Government surveys present this as a financial inclusion success story: adoption is now broadly similar across gender and rural-urban lines, and transaction data is increasingly used to extend formal credit to first-time borrowers who were previously excluded from the banking system. This paper argues that the picture is more layered than the headline numbers suggest. Drawing on official NPCI and Economic Survey data, comparative work on peer systems such as Brazil's Pix and Kenya's M-Pesa, and everyday, lived experience of banking before and after UPI, it traces how UPI reduced the friction of physical banking, examines how it is reshaping access to credit, and then turns a critical eye to what transaction counts conceal: continued heavy reliance on cash, uneven depth of digital participation, and a rising tide of digital fraud that falls hardest on the least digitally literate users. The paper closes by considering UPI as an exportable model, already adopted or being piloted in several countries, and asks what other nations should take from India's experience, including its unresolved problems, before adopting it as a template for their own financial inclusion strategy.

title: Economic Growth in the Theory of Evolutionary Economics: Historical Review

detail.title: Economic Growth in the Theory of Evolutionary Economics: Historical Review
detail.abstract: Economic growth is an integral part of the development of any economic system. With an increase in production capacity and the introduction of innovations, the economy gains additional potential to expand goods production. The key objective of contemporary economic theory is to identify and analyze the root causes of economic growth, as well as to create a unified theory that makes it possible to understand the nature of economic development and, consequently, to put into practice effective development mechanisms. This paper reviews the basic concepts of the theory of evolutionary economic growth. The purpose of the work is to provide a theoretical description of evolutionary processes in economic systems and to analyze the importance of evolutionary economics in the context of economic growth.

title: The Combustion Activation Gap: A Strategic Management Perspective on Energy Inefficiency and Value Erosion

detail.title: The Combustion Activation Gap: A Strategic Management Perspective on Energy Inefficiency and Value Erosion

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests, financial or otherwise, that could have influenced this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a theoretical and illustrative research paper involving no human participants, patient data, case studies, or primary data collection.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Why do chemically controllable combustion systems persistently operate far below their technical efficiency frontier? This paper argues that the answer lies not in chemistry, but in strategic sequencing-a failure to stabilize enabling conditions before committing capital. Drawing on Temporal Capital Theory (TCT), we argue that inefficient combustion can be understood as an Activation Gap: capital is committed to combustion-based infrastructure (t K) before the enabling conditions for complete combustion-fuel quality, skilled operators, maintenance systems, and regulatory oversight-are stabilized (t E). An illustrative analysis of the 2023 World Bank Enterprise Survey data for Tanzania reveals that 60.8% of 600 surveyed firms have adopted energy management measures, yet 47.2% rely on combustion-based generators, and power outages cost businesses an estimated 15% of annual sales. The DICE-Africa emissions inventory is consistent with the view that diffuse and inefficient combustion is a major component of Africa's pollution profile. A case study of Tanzania's largest brewery reveals a boiler operating at 62% efficiency-33 percentage points below the chemically achievable 94-95%. We argue that closing the combustion Activation Gap likely requires strategic sequencing: stabilizing enabling conditions before committing to combustion capital. The paper evaluates policy instruments-Pigouvian taxation, tradable permits, command-and-control regulations, information programs, and subsidies-through a TCT lens, demonstrating that effective intervention must address the temporal ordering of investments. This analysis establishes combustion inefficiency as a strategic management challenge, with implications for energy policy, industrial strategy, and the broader applicability of TCT's sequencing logic across physical, human, and digital capital domains.

title: Congestion-aware Storage Assignment in Parallel-Aisle Warehouses

detail.title: Congestion-aware Storage Assignment in Parallel-Aisle Warehouses
detail.abstract: Turnover-based storage places frequently requested stock near a warehouse depot, but this concentration can send simultaneous pickers to the same narrow aisles. This paper evaluates a storage-assignment rule that trades a distance proxy against an aisle-load penalty. The rule is tested in a synthetic parallel-aisle warehouse using an event-driven simulator, fixed random seeds, common order streams across policies, paired confidence intervals, and contrasting low-interference cases. In the main case, the proposed rule reduces wave makespan relative to both random and turnover-only assignment. The operational mechanism is a reduction in blocking delay that more than offsets a small increase in walking. Factorial results show that the advantage grows with simultaneous-picker load and demand concentration, while single-picker and uniform-demand cases yield near-zero differences. The resulting decision rule is conditional: an aisle-load penalty is valuable when congestion is material, whereas a simpler turnover policy remains suitable when shared-aisle interference is weak. Synthetic inputs, executable scripts, raw results, figures, and manuscript tables accompany the study.

title: From Raw Exports to Value Addition: Do Beneficiation and Trade-integration Policies Raise Manufacturing Value Added in Resource-rich Developing Economies? Panel and Synthetic-control Evidence from Six Countries, 1990–2024
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: From Raw Exports to Value Addition: Do Beneficiation and Trade-integration Policies Raise Manufacturing Value Added in Resource-rich Developing Economies? Panel and Synthetic-control Evidence from Six Countries, 1990–2024
detail.abstract: Resource-rich developing countries increasingly pursue beneficiation and local value-addition policies in the hope of turning mineral and agricultural wealth into a broad manufacturing base. This paper asks whether those strategies raise economy-wide manufacturing value added (MVA). We use a balanced panel of six resource-dependent economies (Botswana, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Indonesia, Malaysia, Zambia, and Zimbabwe) covering 1990 to 2024. In country fixed-effects models with Driscoll-Kraay and cluster-robust standard errors, trade openness is the only stable correlate of the manufacturing share: a one-point rise in exports relative to GDP is associated with roughly 0.09 to 0.10 additional points of MVA/GDP (p < 0.01). Resource-rent dependence, FDI inflows, and the exchange rate show no significant association once country heterogeneity is absorbed. The manufacturing share is also strongly persistent, with an autoregressive coefficient near 0.63, which points to considerable path dependence. A synthetic-control evaluation of Indonesia's 2014 nickel-ore export ban finds no rise in aggregate MVA relative to a data-driven counterfactual (mean post-treatment gap of about-1.3 points; placebo pseudo-p of roughly 0.67). These patterns fit the prematuredeindustrialization thesis and suggest that beneficiation effects, where they exist, sit inside particular processing sub-sectors rather than in the aggregate manufacturing share. We set out the measurement and identification requirements, above all product-level trade-composition data, needed to test the beneficiation hypothesis head-on.

title: Logos Gate Core v0.5: Local Verification Bundles and Restart Cards for Deterministic AI-agent Release Control

detail.title: Logos Gate Core v0.5: Local Verification Bundles and Restart Cards for Deterministic AI-agent Release Control

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the Representative Director of C3 Social Design Center, the organization that developed and operates the Logos Gate Core system evaluated in this paper. All observations reported here were produced and verified by the author using the organization's own implementation and tooling. No independent party produced, replayed, or verified the results. This relationship is stated in the paper itself: the limitations section records that verification was performed on one machine by one operator, and the paper explicitly does not claim third-party validation. Patent applications related to the described architecture have been filed by the author. The author declares no other financial or personal relationships that could have influenced this work.
declarations.funderStatement: This work received no external funding. It was conducted with internal resources of C3 Social Design Center.

detail.abstract:
AI agents increasingly issue requests that cross an external boundary — writing a file, calling a service, changing a configuration, deploying an artifact. Generation and release are different decisions, and a control layer can evaluate the second before it takes effect. Logos Gate Core studies deterministic release control for such requests, emitting a stable verdict, reason codes, and release-token status that can be inspected afterwards. This working paper reports on the layer that operates after a request is stopped: Sea Chart maps a non-PASS record's own reason codes into typed deltas, and Restart Card converts those deltas into re-check preparation gated on restart-context completeness. Post-block paths are common in this area; what is examined here is deriving one from the stopped record rather than selecting a behavior declared when the policy was written.

Three observations are reported over a frozen closed-sandbox baseline of 179 non-PASS records. First, three records stopped at UNDEFINED because a reason code fell outside the delta mapping; in two of them a delta had already been identified, and a single unmapped companion code still forced the whole record to stop. Second, supplying synthetic restart contexts at three pre-registered completeness levels produced 40 re-check candidates at the complete level and none at the partial or absent levels, with release blocked on all 200 cards and byte-identical output across two runs. Third, recomputing all 422 bundle file digests and three manifest digests with an independent hashing implementation produced no mismatches.

The boundaries are specific. The re-check branch was reached under synthetic context only, against a criterion that checks the presence of three fields rather than their content. Recomputation on one machine by one operator is not external verification. This paper does not claim production signing, public-key verification, third-party validation, certification, restart success, or proof of AI-agent safety.

title: Does US Monetary Policy Affect Private Credit in Ecuador? Evidence from a VAR Analysis

detail.title: Does US Monetary Policy Affect Private Credit in Ecuador? Evidence from a VAR Analysis
detail.abstract: This study analyzes the impact of the Federal Reserve's (Fed) monetary policy on the volume of credit to the private sector in Ecuador from January 2014 to October 2023, using econometric time series techniques. Employing a Vector Autoregressive (VAR) model with four lags and Granger causality tests , it assesses whether changes in the federal funds rate affect domestic credit and whether this effect operates through the Ecuadorian Monetary Bond Index (EMBI). Granger causality from the Federal Reserve rate to Ecuadorian credit (p=0.649), contrary to the initial hypothesis. However, significant evidence was found that country risk (p=0.018) and domestic economic activity (p=0.004) do affect credit. Impulse-response functions confirm the absence of significant effects of shocks to the Federal Reserve. These findings suggest that, although Ecuador uses the US dollar, its financial system operates with relative isolation from international markets, responding primarily to domestic factors. This study contributes to the empirical evidence on the limited transmission of international monetary policy in dollarized economies with restricted financial integration.

title: From Complaint to Action: Reforming Nigeria's Public Procurement Oversight Through the Citizen Oversight and Reporting Accountability (CORA) Mechanism
affiliations: and Adeleke University,Ede Osun State

detail.title: From Complaint to Action: Reforming Nigeria's Public Procurement Oversight Through the Citizen Oversight and Reporting Accountability (CORA) Mechanism
detail.abstract: In Akoko-Edo Federal Constituency, ₦65 million was spent on a road that residents could dismantle with their bare hands after construction. Contractors were paid, the project was recorded as completed, yet no citizen had a safe or effective channel to trigger government action. This reflects a broader national pattern as the Bureau of Public Procurement documented over 11,000 abandoned federal projects worth ₦12 trillion. In 2023, Afrobarometer further reports that only 24% of Nigerians trust the federal government. Together, these point to a systemic breakdown in procurement accountability and enforcement in Nigeria. The Public Procurement Act 2007 established the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP) with mandates for contract certification, audits, and citizen complaints under Section 38. However, this system was designed for formal complainants, not ordinary citizens and it has no automatic enforcement trigger linked to citizen reports.  This paper evaluates three policy options: Complaint Access & Process Enhancement (CAPE), Citizen Oversight & Reporting Accountability (CORA), and Supplier Compliance & Oversight Rating (SCOR). CORA is recommended as the most feasible option. It is a regulatory upgrade under Section 4 of the Public Procurement Act, requiring no new legislation. It also enables anonymous reporting through USSD, mobile, and web platforms in five Nigerian languages. When reports reach a set threshold, they trigger a Bureau of Public Procurement audit, with findings published within 30 days. By linking citizen reporting to mandatory action, CORA is designed to rebuild institutional trust between citizens and Nigeria's public procurement institutions.

title: Policy, Legislative and Oversight Measures Required for Integrating New Technologies in Counter-Terrorism

detail.title: Policy, Legislative and Oversight Measures Required for Integrating New Technologies in Counter-Terrorism

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing personal or financial interests that could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Drawing on field experience and stakeholder engagement across the Security Sector Reform, parliamentary development and new technologies domain, this paper examines the dual role of parliaments in responding to the use of emerging technologies in Counter-Terrorism. Artificial intelligence and other machine-learning technologies offer new means for law-enforcement and parliamentary oversight, while simultaneously introducing vulnerabilities that can be exploited by terrorist actors for propaganda, recruitment, financing and cyberattacks on parliaments and Members of Parliament (MPs). Parliaments bear legislative and oversight responsibility for ensuring that security agencies remain effective and rights-compliant, but many legislatures and legislators face significant gaps in their technical knowledge and access to comparative best-practice. This concept note proposes a two-tier training model, that is specialized training for MPs and staff directly engaged in counter-terrorism, and baseline training for all parliamentarians, supported by guiding principles and best practices to strengthen MPs' awareness of legislation and oversight that uphold international human rights and humanitarian law. Its aim is to strengthen legislative capacity, support parliamentary staff, enhance inter-parliamentary cooperation and promote transparent, accountable and democratically grounded national responses to the challenges posed by the use and abuse of these emerging technologies.

title: Labour Vulnerability and Climate Shocks among Low-Skilled Workers in India: Evidence from PLFS, IMD (Satellite Climate Data) and Spatial Econometrics Analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Labour Vulnerability and Climate Shocks among Low-Skilled Workers in India: Evidence from PLFS, IMD (Satellite Climate Data) and Spatial Econometrics Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study utilizes publicly available, anonymized secondary datasets and does not involve human participants or animal experiments.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Climate Change is reshaping rural labour markets in India. Recent climate anomalies, such as extreme heat waves and early or delayed monsoon seasons, are pushing Low-Skilled Marginal rural labourers to shift from Agriculture to Non-Agricultural sectors in India. While The Classical Structural Transformation Theory suggests that the voluntary labour transition from agriculture to non-agricultural sectors can improve economic growth, labour productivity and welfare, this study argues that climate-induced low-skilled marginal labourers are pushed into distress-driven survival and further pushed into vulnerability, resulting in work on a low and irregular wage pattern affecting their Income and Employment. This study examines shocks and labour vulnerability among low-skilled rural workers in India influenced by Climate factors and forced into multidimensional Labour Vulnerability. To examine this relationship, a harmonized Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) panel spanning 2022-2025, combined with India Meteorological Department (IMD) gridded climate data. A four-pillar Labour Vulnerability Index (LVI) is constructed at the district-year level, covering Employment Security, Income Security, Underemployment, and Sectoral Vulnerability it employs district-level spatial analysis (Global Moran's I, LISA) Spatial Autoregressive (SAR) and Spatial Error Model (SEM) to observe both direct and spillover effects. Two complementary empirical strategies are employed. First, a two-way fixed effects panel model finds no statistically significant relationship between extreme heat or rainfall shocks and the composite LVI or its Income Security pillar, a null result that is robust to a one-year lag specification. Second, a district-level spatial econometric analysis - Global Moran's I, Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA), Spatial Autoregressive (SAR), and Spatial Error (SEM) models - reveals strong, statistically significant spatial clustering in the LVI in every survey year (Moran's I 0.34-0.43, p<0.01), and a statistically significant positive association between extreme heat days and the LVI once spatial dependence is properly modelled, replicated across all four years. At the individual level, extreme heat exposure is associated with a small but significant shift in employment insecurity, substantially moderated by gender in a direction opposite to the amplification hypothesis originally proposed. These findings show that climate-labour vulnerability in India is not simply a matter of a district's own year-to-year climate exposure, but is embedded in a strongly spatially clustered structure in which neighbouring districts' labour markets and climate conditions are closely linked. This distinction between within-district temporal effects and cross-district spatial effects is itself a substantive contribution, and points to regional, coordinated policy responses rather than purely district-targeted interventions. This study contributes to the growing literature on climate change and labour economics by combining granular microdata with district-level climate records and reporting results transparently, including null findings, rather than selectively emphasizing only statistically significant results. The findings have implications for how climate-labour research designs choose their unit of aggregation and time horizon, and for the specific channels - rather than a uniform vulnerability effect - through which climate exposure interacts with gender in India's informal rural labour market.

title: Analysis of the Macroenvironmental Impact on the Banking Sector of Ukraine
affiliations: Kyiv National Economic University (KNEU)

detail.title: Analysis of the Macroenvironmental Impact on the Banking Sector of Ukraine
detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the structural performance and developmental trajectory of the Ukrainian banking services market through a macro-environmental analytical lens. Utilizing a structured PEST framework (Political, Economic, Socio-cultural, and Technological), the study investigates the direct and indirect influence of macro-level drivers on banking stability and commercial operations. The research systematically delineates key strategic opportunities and systemic market threats generated by the external environment. Based on these empirical and environmental findings, the paper formulates actionable recommendations for recalibrating bank marketing strategies to ensure institutional resilience and sustainable competitive positioning in a volatile financial landscape.

title:
From Regime Boundaries to Chemical Gauge Group: The Inevitable Emergence of the Periodic Law and the Cross-Disciplinary Unification of the Factor Hierarchy Law
——Derivation of the Chemical Gauge Group Theorem, the Chemical Counterpart of the Higgs Mechanism, and the Establishment of the Five-Layer Axiomatic Structure (III)

detail.title:
From Regime Boundaries to Chemical Gauge Group: The Inevitable Emergence of the Periodic Law and the Cross-Disciplinary Unification of the Factor Hierarchy Law
——Derivation of the Chemical Gauge Group Theorem, the Chemical Counterpart of the Higgs Mechanism, and the Establishment of the Five-Layer Axiomatic Structure (III)
detail.abstract: Why are there exactly four types of atomic orbitals—s, p, d, and f? Why does the periodic table have an end? What is the relationship between the Factor Hierarchy Law, quantum mechanics, and gauge field theory? Building on the empirical discoveries of the two preceding papers, this paper completes three core theoretical derivations that elevate the periodic law from an empirical regularity to an inevitable deduction from first principles. First derivation: the Chemical Gauge Group Theorem. The meta-regime factor valence_electrons possesses n=8 mutually exclusive regime states (outermost electron numbers = 1, 2, …, 8), and its moderating effects cover all executive factors with irreducible interaction effects. Under the symmetry constraint of the three-dimensional rotation group SO(3), the unique group-theoretic correspondence of the eight regime states is the l=0, 1, 2, 3 irreducible representations of SO(3)—namely, the s, p, d, and f orbitals. The sum of the dimensions of these irreducible representations is 1+3+5+7=16, exactly corresponding to eight spin-degenerate regime states. No regime state with l≥4 exists, because the l=4 representation is 9-dimensional, corresponding to 18 spin-orbitals, far exceeding the capacity of eight regime states, and the required nuclear charge number would exceed the nuclear stability limit. Second derivation: the division of labor and subsumption between the Factor Hierarchy Law and quantum mechanics. The Factor Hierarchy Law provides the regime-state structure (the eight mutually exclusive regime states of valence_electrons), and quantum mechanics provides the symmetry constraint (the underlying symmetry of electron configuration is SO(3)). Together, they derive the inevitability of s, p, d, and f orbitals. This is not “dependence” on quantum mechanics but rather the demotion of quantum mechanics from a “fundamental theory” to “a provider of symmetry constraints as physical input”—completely isomorphic in logical structure to the “demotion of gauge field theory” in Tang (2026q). Third derivation: the end of the periodic table. The topological constraints of transition bandwidths determine the upper limit of the number of regime centers. As the orbital angular momentum l increases, the spacing between regime centers expands exponentially. The entrance to the g-block (l=4) at Z≈121 is the last detectable regime center. The nuclear charge number required for the entrance to the h-block (l=5) exceeds the nuclear stability limit—the fission barrier height drops below 1 MeV, and any heavier nuclide would fission at the moment of formation. The end of the periodic table is not an arbitrary human stipulation but the inevitable joint consequence of topological constraints from regime centers and the physical limits of nuclear stability. Integrating these three derivations, this paper establishes the five-layer axiomatic structure of the regime-switching theory of the periodic law—Law Layer (three axioms) → Norm Layer (six functional dimensions) → Algorithm Layer (three-step MRSD logic) → Theorem and Proposition Layer (four quantitative laws + the Chemical Gauge Group Theorem) → Theory Layer (nine cross-disciplinary corollaries). This structure is completely isomorphic to the five-layer structure established by Tang (2026q) in particle physics. The Factor Hierarchy Law emerged from financial data, was verified in stellar atmospheres, obtained its mathematical foundation in statistical physics, derived gauge group structures in particle physics, and completed the demotion of fundamental laws in chemistry—it is not the law of a single discipline but the universal logic of the functional stratification of variables in any complex system based on objective data.

title: Market Prism: A State-Space Framework for Structural Mispricing, Narrative Decay, and Sector Energy Reallocation in Equity Markets

detail.title: Market Prism: A State-Space Framework for Structural Mispricing, Narrative Decay, and Sector Energy Reallocation in Equity Markets
detail.abstract: Standard asset-pricing practice treats short-horizon price innovations as Gaussian noise about a random walk, which leaves no operational way to separate sustainable value from structural mispricing; in parallel, the narrative content of markets is typically reduced to static sentiment scores that ignore how quickly belief decays. This paper introduces Market Prism, a state-space measurement framework that makes both quantities explicit. First, we fix an absolute fundamental reference frame (V ground) derived from audited regulatory disclosures and measure the displacement of the spot price from that frame as a positioning error (Δ)-an approach we describe by analogy to satellite positioning rather than dead-reckoning momentum. Second, we quantify narrative decay by fitting exponential constants (λ) to narrative intensity over the post-earnings opacity window, organized by an information-thermodynamic analogy that yields a falsifiable prediction about volatility at the disclosure boundary. Third, we formalize a sector energy reallocation principle under which speculative intensity evicted from one name migrates laterally to related names. Fourth, we integrate four traditionally siloed domains-forensic disclosure verification, Bayesian source credibility with decay, options microstructure, and fundamental valuation-into a single 79-field cross-domain schema over a point-in-time panel of approximately 244 million populated cells (282 relational tables; 10.5 million rows). We evaluate the resulting signals with institutional-grade safeguards: two-way (date×ticker) clustered inference (aggregate t = 4.47), Newey-West HAC inference for the flagship sector-rotation signal (t = 4.02, positive in each of three annual regimes), the Deflated Sharpe Ratio (99.6-100% for the live execution book), and White's Reality Check / Hansen's SPA multiple-testing controls (p = 0.0075 and p = 0.0125, respectively). The evidence indicates a small but statistically robust, largely market-neutral edge that is concentrated at the sector level. We are explicit throughout that the physical vocabulary is an organizing analogy, not a claim of literal physical law, and we delineate the boundary conditions, attribution limits, and open questions.

title: No Better Than Random: An Agent-Level Reality Check for LLM Factor Selection

detail.title: No Better Than Random: An Agent-Level Reality Check for LLM Factor Selection
detail.abstract: Do LLM agents that select among published return-predictor signals find genuine structure, or do they simply benefit from evaluating many candidates and reporting the best? We treat a complete agent pipeline, including proposal, evaluation, self-screening and iterative adaptation, as a single stochastic strategy-selection rule, and compute the finite-sample distribution of its headline statistic under a null that demeans each signal's return series and resamples time jointly across signals via a stationary bootstrap. Across 200 closed-loop agent runs on null panels drawn from 183 published long-short predictor portfolios, the agent's observed Sharpe ratio of 0.617 exceeds all 200 null draws (p = 0.0050, 15.2 null standard deviations above the null mean). By this test alone the agent appears to be finding something real. A budget-matched control overturns that reading. Running best-of-N blind random search over the same candidate space at the same evaluation budgets, the agent's mean performance is statistically indistinguishable from random search at every budget tested (z from-0.06 to 1.35). The apparent skill the Reality Check alone would credit to the agent is instead attributable to publication selection in its candidate universe and to the multiplicity of evaluating many candidates and keeping the best. Every standard multiple-testing correction we test is itself miscalibrated under agentic search, with empirical size at nominal 5% ranging from 1.5% to 84.5%. Reported performance for such agents should be benchmarked against both an agent-level null and a budget-matched random-search control; a result that clears the first but not the second is not evidence of agent skill.

title: Strategic Petroleum Stockholding, Two-way Trade and Energy Security: An Inter-regional Computable General Equilibrium Analysis for Indonesia
affiliations: Padjadjaran University - Faculty of Economics and Business

detail.title: Strategic Petroleum Stockholding, Two-way Trade and Energy Security: An Inter-regional Computable General Equilibrium Analysis for Indonesia

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: No funder available

detail.abstract: Indonesia faces a structural energy security challenge: it holds roughly three weeks of fuel reserves against an international 90-day norm and struggles to attract private capital into petroleum storage. Using an 8-region, 20-sector computable general equilibrium (CGE) model spanning 2016–2035, this paper demonstrates that without capacity additions, Indonesia’s dependence on refined fuel imports will quadruple. While enforcing a strict 90-day stockholding mandate acts as a drag on GDP, demand-side biofuel mandates (B40) outperform major refinery expansions in reducing import reliance without requiring heavy infrastructure investment.

title: The Depth of the Conditions of Life

detail.title: The Depth of the Conditions of Life

declarations.ethicsApproval: I have used artificial intelligence to find sources, organize and finalize the text.

detail.abstract: This article joins a critique of financial depth to a methodological account of knowing and making under conditions of ecological interdependence. Financial depth is commonly treated as a measure of liquidity, risk distribution, and allocative efficiency. The article argues that this interpretation mistakes the proliferation of claims upon the future for the reproduction of the conditions through which such claims could be realized. It proposes a 4 × 4 × 4 grammar of commoning reproduction: four depths (temporal, referential, institutional, scalar), four irreducible ledgers (financial, energy, material-ecological, time), and four civilizational functions (Schole, Polis, Oikos, Agora). The grammar is not an optimization device. It is a constitutional method for asking whether a proposed relation is materially viable, publicly intelligible, democratically authorized, and fairly distributed. A mimetic-metic ecology of knowing and making connects language, numerical models, situated practice, and correction without reducing one to another. Artificial intelligence is accordingly treated as politically subordinate computational infrastructure. Appendix A formalizes the grammar; Appendix B nests it within planetary-boundary constraints; and Appendix C applies it to an AI-assisted public-housing retrofit.

title: The Double-Slit Correspondence: Structural Cascade Governance for Multi-Agent AI — Part Two: The Cascade

detail.title: The Double-Slit Correspondence: Structural Cascade Governance for Multi-Agent AI — Part Two: The Cascade
detail.abstract: Part One of this paper established a five-parameter governance correspondence for a single AI governance layer: when two agents are trained on a MECE-compliant source and deployed with genuine architectural distinctness, every detector — internal risk team, board, regulator — sees the same underlying structure simultaneously. Part One closed with a question it could not answer: what happens to that guarantee when the output of one layer becomes the input for the next? This paper answers that question. Applying Huygens' principle to the cascade, it shows that a non-MECE failure at any layer corrupts every downstream layer simultaneously, without any individual agent detecting it. When a downstream layer's own data is rich enough to partially mask the upstream failure, the cascade output appears acceptable in normal conditions and fails only under stress: the paper names this governance moral hazard. The central result is the Cascade Proposition: MECE certification at every layer and at every transition between layers is the structural guarantee for the entire cascade. A general recursive structural exposure formula, parameterised by each layer's own MECE gap g_n, handoff resolution factor f_n, and upstream dependency weight w_n, makes this precise and establishes the joint obligation: the CDO and CRO cannot certify the cascade independently, and every transition between layers requires explicit governance sign-off. The paper then extends this to the stochastic case. When governance parameters are uncertain — as they always are in practice — the structural exposure recurrence becomes a random affine recurrence. Drawing on Brandt (1986) and Bougerol (1993), the paper proves that a unique stationary distribution for structural exposure G* exists and is reached exponentially fast. The correct certification target is the second-moment condition E[α_n²] < 1: a cascade can satisfy mean(α) < 1 while its risk tail diverges toward certain structural failure. The CRO's obligation follows: declare a tail threshold τ before inspecting the stationary distribution, not after. Dataset shift is shown to be a structural consequence of the cascade architecture itself; setting τ after observing the distribution is the tail-risk equivalent of the Fresnel Excuse.

title: The Mirror Glut: The Wage Commons in the Open Economy

detail.title: The Mirror Glut: The Wage Commons in the Open Economy
detail.abstract: The closed-economy escape path from joint labor-share suppression and public-debt accumulation (Goren 2026i) survives opening, but every leg changes size and two change ownership. Opening the model does four things. First, the certification statistic that separates healing from harmful inflation must be read on product prices, not consumer prices: imported disinflation drives a terms-of-trade wedge between the two, and a CPI-read certificate fires falsely in both directions. Second, the inflation levy gains a foreign-held leg. With roughly a third of publicly held U.S. debt in foreign hands, the escape path partially exports the levy, taxing foreign holders without a treaty; the offsets are repricing, as in the closed economy, plus a cost the closed economy does not have, erosion of the convenience yield that lets the debt be issued cheaply in the first place. Third, the global savings glut is the wage commons run globally: the wage commons is the externality by which wage suppression is a private gain funded by a public cost, and wage generosity a private cost funding a public gain (Goren 2026a), and labor-share suppression in surplus economies returns as captive demand for the American outside asset, flattening the neutral rate's response to the domestic labor share and deepening the trap steady state. The foreign leg of the escape path is therefore financed by the uncorrected commons abroad and depletes as it is corrected: a wasting asset. Fourth, profit shifting drains the rent base that carries the permanent consolidation, pulling the fiscal-dominance frontier inward, so international tax coordination is commitment infrastructure and its absence is anti-commitment infrastructure. The paper closes with an admission test for open-economy instruments: an instrument enhances the escape path only if it does not corrupt the certificate, does not tax the recovering base, and extends the levy or shifts the frontier outward. Tariffs fail the first two tests on the measured incidence of the recent U.S. episodes, and the tariff-revenue defense fails with them: to the extent pass-through into home prices is near complete, the revenue is collected by compressing the real wage, so tariffs tax the commons. Capital controls and financial repression pass all three when gated on the certificate and sunset-dated, and in the open economy they are more than an enhancement: without management of the capital-flow margin, the held-rate tolerance window may not be feasible at all. They tax the mirror, collecting the levy off captivity without touching the wage statistic, at the price of a higher discretionary temptation if retained. The correction of the wage commons is a positive-sum export: foreign labor-share recovery shrinks the mirror term and helps the domestic exit, the inverse of the tariff logic the admission test rejects.

title: Shifting Patterns in Global Flows of Trade, Capital, Migration and Information

detail.title: Shifting Patterns in Global Flows of Trade, Capital, Migration and Information
detail.abstract:
Since the beginning of time, the world's economies have been interconnected. These connections have ranged from simple partnerships to complex exchanges of resources. Throughout human history, no country has ever possessed all the resources it needed, making international connections essential. People, trade, capital, and information have always been the key flows driving global interaction, although their evolution varies depending on the global context. In an ever-changing international system shaped by economic, political, and social factors, these flows shift in scale and direction but consistently remain the forces that keep states connected.

 Economic flows are reflected in the export and import of goods and services, migration (i.e., the movement of people), technology transfer, information exchange, innovation, foreign direct investment, and the operations of transnational corporations. Without these components, the global economy cannot function effectively, increasing the risk of widening gaps between countries or even their isolation. Therefore, international economic flows are essential for global growth, the development of partnerships, diversification of supply sources, market expansion, and job creation. They are the engine of growth and development. This article aims to identify the defining features of each type of flow and to demonstrate the importance of the global economic circuit they create. By analysing trade, migration, capital, and technology flows, the paper will justify their critical role in the economies of all countries, regardless of their level of development.

title: Money, Time, and the Limits of Abstraction: A Brief on Monetary Multiplicity and the Velocity Mismatch

detail.title: Money, Time, and the Limits of Abstraction: A Brief on Monetary Multiplicity and the Velocity Mismatch
detail.abstract: This brief examines money's dual ontology-physical currency and credit creation-and analyzes how the temporal mediating function of interest has eroded under conditions of extreme monetary abstraction. It argues that a structural velocity mismatch has emerged between the exponential logic of financial time and the cyclical rhythms of natural and social reproduction, producing systemic strain that conventional macroeconomic models fail to capture.

title: Capturing Local Growth: The Economic and Environmental Impact of the Common Agricultural Policy on Areas with Natural Constraints
affiliations: Department of Statistical Sciences, University of Bologna,  and Department of Statistical Sciences, University of Bologna

detail.title: Capturing Local Growth: The Economic and Environmental Impact of the Common Agricultural Policy on Areas with Natural Constraints
detail.abstract: The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) is one of the world's largest agricultural programs, yet causal evidence on its effects remains limited because of policy endogeneity. We exploit the implementation framework and eligibility criteria introduced in Italy in 2020 for support to areas facing natural constraints, which generate a setting that approximates a natural experiment. Drawing on a rich dataset and a sound counterfactual approach, we find that subsidies increased agricultural employment, especially in the most subsidized areas, improved production efficiency, encouraged environmental certifications, reduced the use of polluting inputs, modestly slowed rural depopulation, and pointed to positive local economic spillovers.

title: The Hidden Demand: Extending the JD-R Model to Include Assessment Ethics Pressure and Its Impact on Teacher Retention in Pakistan
affiliations: The Smart School

detail.title: The Hidden Demand: Extending the JD-R Model to Include Assessment Ethics Pressure and Its Impact on Teacher Retention in Pakistan
detail.abstract: Teacher attrition is a persistent challenge in Pakistan’s education system. While the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model effectively explains burnout through workload and resources, it has paid less attention to demands rooted in professional ethics. This conceptual paper introduces Assessment Ethics Pressure (AEP) as a distinct job demand. AEP refers to the psychological strain teachers experience when external assessment mandates conflict with their professional standards for fairness and validity. Drawing on JD-R theory, scholarship on moral distress, and literature on high-stakes testing, I argue that AEP contributes to exhaustion and turnover intention beyond traditional demands. The discussion is grounded in the Pakistani context, where BISE board examinations carry high public visibility and institutional consequences. The paper concludes with implications for teacher education, school leadership, and policy, and outlines directions for future empirical work.

title: Reimagining China's Bhutan Policy

detail.title: Reimagining China's Bhutan Policy
detail.abstract: Current literature analysing China-Bhutan relations overlooks historical memory as a factor shaping China’s engagement with Bhutan. This article argues that China's neighbourhood policy is not simply about managing borders but also about shaping a regional environment that is consistent with Beijing's understanding of its own identity.

title: The Modified Gerber Statistic: A Practical Nonparametric Covariance Estimator for Portfolio Construction
affiliations: Hudson Bay Capital Management, LP, Imperial College London, University of California at San Diego, , Imperial College London, Ulster University, Hudson Bay Capital Management, LP and Hudson Bay Capital Management, LP

detail.title: The Modified Gerber Statistic: A Practical Nonparametric Covariance Estimator for Portfolio Construction
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Modified Gerber Statistic (MGS), a threshold-free co-movement statistic for covariance estimation and portfolio construction. The original Gerber statistic counts same-and oppositedirection joint moves only after both assets cross selected thresholds. MGS instead uses a nonparametric rank transformation: it ranks each observation relative to the asset's own history and uses every observation, giving the most influence to episodes in which both assets occupy similarly unusual states and less influence to one-sided events. This limits the effect of extreme raw values, makes unlike assets and signals comparable, and produces a covariance input that can enter an existing portfolio optimizer. We compare MGS with the original Gerber statistic, Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage, and historical covariance in two out-of-sample studies from January 1990 through December 2025. In the 10-asset study, MGS has the highest annualized geometric return at every displayed target-risk level from 3% through 15%. At the 9% target, MGS earns 11.26%, compared with 11.04% for the original Gerber statistic, 10.92% for shrinkage, and 11.05% for historical covariance. An equal-weight return-plus-four-week-divergence illustration reduces realized volatility, maximum drawdown, and turnover in every sleeve; at the 15% target, it raises geometric return from 15.17% to 15.38% and reduces maximum drawdown from-42.71% to-40.01%. In a monthly study of the point-in-time 30 largest S&P 500 constituents, return-only MGS has the highest geometric return among the four core estimators and a higher Sharpe ratio than the original Gerber statistic at every displayed target from 3% through 21%. At the 9% target, return-only MGS earns 9.15% with a 0.57 Sharpe ratio, compared with 8.42% and 0.55 for the original Gerber statistic. Combining return and trend-divergence evidence raises these figures to 9.76% and 0.60. The results support MGS as a practical co-movement estimator and show how managers can incorporate additional evidence about correlation without changing the portfolio construction workflow.

title: When and How Can You Correct for Spatial Autocorrelation?

detail.title: When and How Can You Correct for Spatial Autocorrelation?
detail.abstract: Spatial social science often relies on expanding domain asymptotics in which growth in the number of rows of data n comes (at least partly) from the geographic area of study growing. This paper asks whether growth in n from finer partitions of a fixed geographic area T can recover a chosen population-or area-weighted average effect. I study a benchmark linear model Y (t) = X(t) ′ β(t) + ε(t) with spatially correlated explanatory variables X(t) and Gaussian process errors ε(t) at each point in space t ∈ T. The main identification result states that, in order to identify \int β(t) dµ(t), X(t) must be sufficiently "coarse" and β(t) must be sufficiently "smooth" so that variation in Y (t) can be attributed to the signal X(t) ′ β(t) as opposed to the noise ε(t). Under stronger assumptions, I propose weights for the small regions and show how to report spatial uncertainty separately from approximation error.

title: Skilled Informal Labor in Platform Economy in Pakistan- A Policy Analysis of (Draft) National Freelancing Facilitation Policy 2021

detail.title: Skilled Informal Labor in Platform Economy in Pakistan- A Policy Analysis of (Draft) National Freelancing Facilitation Policy 2021
detail.abstract: Online freelancing can add great value to Pakistan's overall economic growth and provide youth employment opportunities. But the absence of a nationally implemented policy or a facilitating framework undermines this potential. This study explores issues faced by freelancers in Pakistan and evaluates whether the draft policy caters to Pakistan's freelancers' requirements. The research design of this dissertation has been kept descriptive and exploratory. In light of the experiences of freelancers around the world and supportive national policies, qualitative methodology is used to evaluate the (draft) National Freelancing Facilitation Policy 2021 based on a devised analytical framework. Results indicate that while the policy is quite comprehensive, it does not adequately cater for documentation, banking services, taxation, access to financial capital, access to infrastructure, training, and skill development. It is recommended to create a public-private partnership to resolve these issues.

title: KDI 경제동향 2026. 7 (KDI Monthly Economic Trends 2026. 7)

detail.title: KDI 경제동향 2026. 7 (KDI Monthly Economic Trends 2026. 7)

publicationDetails.journalName: Korea Development Institute (KDI) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Korean Abstract: 
■ 우리 경제는 제조업생산이 조정되었으나, 반도체 수출과 서비스업 호조에 힘입어 완만한 개선 흐름을 유지 　
 
 ○ 수출은 견조한 AI 관련 수요에 힘입어 반도체 등 ICT 품목을 중심으로 높은 증가세를 지속하였으며, 반도체 관련 투자도 양호한 흐름을 이어감.
  
  - 반도체 수출물량의 증가세는 조정되었으나, 가격 상승세로 수출금액 기준으로는 호조세 유지
 
 ○ 서비스업생산은 금융보험업과 전문과학기술서비스업을 중심으로 높은 상승세를 이어가며 전산업생산의 증가세를 뒷받침
  
  - 소비가 완만한 증가세를 이어간 가운데, 이와 밀접한 서비스업생산도 개선
 
 ○ 다만, 제조업생산은 반도체의 높았던 증가세가 조정되는 가운데, 여타 부문도 미약한 흐름을 보이며 소폭 감소

English Abstract: 
■ Korea’s economy remained on a modest recovery path, supported by robust semiconductor exports and services activity, while manufacturing production softened.
 
 ○ Exports continued to expand strongly in value terms, led by ICT products such as semiconductors amid robust AI-related demand. Investment in semiconductor-related sectors also remained solid.

  - Although growth in semiconductor export volumes moderated, exports remained robust in value terms, supported by continued price increases.

 ○ Services production continued to rise strongly, led by finance and insurance and professional, scientific, and technical services, supporting growth in total industrial production.
 
  - With consumption rising modestly, activity in consumer-facing service industries also improved.

 ○ However, manufacturing production edged down as the earlier rapid gains in semiconductors moderated and other segments remained subdued.

title: Delegating Corporate Finance to AI: Contract Power and Oversight
affiliations: Hanyang University and Department of Fintech, SKK Business School, Sungkyunkwan University

detail.title: Delegating Corporate Finance to AI: Contract Power and Oversight
detail.abstract: AI-agent firms use autonomous systems both to run operations and to generate the machineverifiable records that support borrowing. Financing contracts written on those records can therefore also function as operating instructions. We study what happens when a firm delegates financing choices to an AI controller. The firm raises funds against archived verified information, through contracts tied to live operating metrics, and through residual finance. We define contract power as the sensitivity of financing terms to a live metric. A fully internalizing owner limits this power because it induces metric targeting at the expense of broader firm value. A delegated controller internalizes only part of that loss and values continued funding access, so it chooses strictly greater contract power at a given financing quantity. In a linear-quadratic benchmark with slack archived capacity, delegation changes financing composition while leaving the amount raised unchanged. Delegation may nevertheless be optimal because autonomous execution creates speed-and-scale benefits, whereas continuously updating oversight and state-contingent corrective rules is costly. Oversight, accountability, internal charges, and power caps reduce the resulting wedge. Better verification need not reduce it, while shared verification infrastructure creates a systemic over-pledging externality across firms.

title: Enhancing the Effectiveness of the Long-Term Care Insurance System
affiliations: Korea Development Institute (KDI)

detail.title: Enhancing the Effectiveness of the Long-Term Care Insurance System

publicationDetails.journalName: Korea Development Institute (KDI) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Korea’s rapid aging has brought the pressing policy concern of social hospitalization to the forefront. Older adults with low medical but high long-term care needs often occupy beds in high-cost medical institutions for extended periods―a trend that is driving up elderly medical spending. In 2008, the government introduced the Long-Term Care Insurance (LTCI) system to address the growing demand for care among older adults and improve their quality of life, while curbing inefficient medical spending. Since then, long-term care services have expanded in both eligibility and scope. The original three-grade classification was restructured into a six-grade system encompassing older adults with mild dementia, and home-based benefits were strengthened as part of a broader shift from facility-centered to home-centered care.

This study uses the Elderly Cohort Database of the National Health Insurance Service to examine how expanding LTCI affects medical expenditures. For identification, it employs a fuzzy regression discontinuity design and an event study design, exploiting the fact that LTCI grades are assigned based on the Long-Term Care Need Score and that the costs and benefits of these grade assignments shift exogenously around each threshold.

Comparing first-time applicants near each grade threshold, the analysis finds that, for Grades 1 and 2, which correspond to greater care needs, the expansion of either facility-based or home-based benefits reduced medical facility utilization and medical expenditures. By institution type, expenditures declined at hospital-level institutions and long-term care hospitals; by utilization type, inpatient costs decreased. For Grades 3 through 5, by contrast, expanding home-based benefits did not have a statistically meaningful effect on reducing medical expenditures. The event study results show that for the Cognitive Support Grade, which covers older adults with mild dementia, expanded home-based benefits lowered medical expenditures.

These results suggest that the effect of LTCI on medical expenditures may be heterogeneous across grades. Particularly for Grades 3 through 5, the quantity and quality of home-based services may have been insufficient to provide the integrated support to meet complex needs for both medical and long-term care. For the Cognitive Support Grade, however, beneficiaries face fewer physical constraints compared to those with greater care needs. This allows easier access to cost-efficient services such as Day and Night Care Centers for extended hours, which may explain the relatively larger reduction in medical expenditures.

Based on these findings, the study proposes policy measures for improving the quality of home-based care through the integration of medical and long-term care services. In particular, drawing primarily on international case studies, it offers recommendations to ensure the stable and effective implementation of the Integrated Care Support System scheduled for 2026. These measures include introducing intermediate long-term care facilities capable of providing a continuum of medical and long-term care services; developing a specialized workforce to ensure the smooth operation of the new framework; optimizing the expansion of this workforce in depopulating regions; and clarifying accountability for social hospitalization among stakeholders to improve the efficiency of medical expenditures.

title: Optimal Transfer Learning for High-Frequency Prediction by Local Cross-validation
affiliations: Singapore Management University, Singapore Management University, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science (AMSS) and Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences

detail.title: Optimal Transfer Learning for High-Frequency Prediction by Local Cross-validation
detail.abstract: Empiricists frequently encounter multiple plausible forecasts for high-frequency data, arising from disparate information sets, alternative statistical approaches, and substantial cross-sectional heterogeneity. We propose a transfer learning approach through high frequency ensemble learning (Transfer-HFEL) that optimally combines forecasts from heterogeneous populations within a state-space framework using a novel local L-fold cross validation criterion. We establish the asymptotic optimality and consistency of the Transfer-HFEL under regularity conditions, and evaluate its performance through simulation studies and an empirical application to ETF data. Empirically, Transfer-HFEL improves predictive accuracy relative to competing methods, delivering an annualized return and Sharpe ratio exceeding the Fama-French three-factor model by 79% and 65%, respectively. Interestingly, transferring idiosyncratic variation across assets yields greater forecasting improvements than transferring common systematic factors. One possible explanation is that model misspecification, time-varying risk premia and microstructure frictions contain valuable information overlooked by parameter-transferred methods. Rather than introducing noise, this idiosyncratic variation provides new insights into return predictability and portfolio performance in high-frequency markets.

title: KDI 경제전망, 2026 상반기 (KDI Economic Outlook, 2026 1st Half)
affiliations: Korea Development Institute (KDI)

detail.title: KDI 경제전망, 2026 상반기 (KDI Economic Outlook, 2026 1st Half)

publicationDetails.journalName: Korea Development Institute (KDI) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Korean Abstract: 
■ 우리 경제는 2026년에 반도체수출 호조세와 내수 개선세로 2.5% 정도 성장한 후, 2027년에도 1.7% 수준의 성장을 나타낼 전망　

- 소비자물가는 국제유가 상승에 경기 회복세가 더해지면서 금년에 2.7% 정도 상승한 후, 내년에는 국제유가 하락에 따라 2.2% 정도로 상승폭이 일부 축소될 전망

- 민간소비는 중동 전쟁에 따른 물가 상승에도 불구하고 소득 개선과 정부 지원 정책에 힘입어 금년과 내년에 각각 2.2%, 1.5% 정도 증가하며 회복세를 보일 전망

- 설비투자는 대외 여건 악화로 반도체를 제외한 부문의 미약한 흐름에도 불구하고 반도체 호조세에 따른 높은 투자 수요로 금년과 내년에 각각 3.3%, 2.4% 정도의 비교적 높은 증가율을 기록할 것으로 예상됨.

- 건설투자는 중동 전쟁에 따른 공사비 상승으로 회복이 지연됨에 따라 금년에 미미하게 증가(0.1%)하다가 내년에는 1.1% 정도로 증가세가 확대될 전망

- 경상수지는 반도체 수출액 급증에 따라 이례적 수준의 대규모 흑자가 전망

English Abstract: 

■ The Korean economy is projected to grow by around 2.5% in 2026, supported by robust semiconductor exports and a recovery in domestic demand, with growth expected at about 1.7% in 2027.
 
- Headline inflation is forecast to rise to around 2.7% in 2026, as higher international oil prices coincide with a recovery in economic activity, before moderating to about 2.2% in 2027 as oil prices decline.
