title: Socioeconomic, biological, and behavioral determinants of gastric cancer incidence and mortality in Latin America and the Caribbean: a sex-stratified ecological study with projections to 2050
affiliations: Universidad de Antioquia, Universidad de Antioquia and Universidad de Antioquia

detail.title: Socioeconomic, biological, and behavioral determinants of gastric cancer incidence and mortality in Latin America and the Caribbean: a sex-stratified ecological study with projections to 2050
detail.abstract: Background. Gastric cancer imposes a heavy, geographically uneven burden across Latin America and the Caribbean. We quantified the associations of socioeconomic, biological, and behavioral factors with gastric cancer incidence and mortality across the region, examined sex-specific patterns and the projected burden to 2050.Methods. A cross-sectional ecological study used the country as the unit of analysis. Age-standardized incidence and mortality rates for 2022 were drawn from the Global Cancer Observatory; behavioral and dietary exposures from the Global Burden of Disease 2021 study; socioeconomic indicators from the United Nations Development Programme; health expenditure from the World Health Organization; and Helicobacter pylori prevalence from a global systematic review. Ordinary least squares models with robust standard errors were fitted by sex, with false discovery rate correction. Projections of cases and deaths to 2050 were examined.Results. The burden was geographically heterogeneous, with the highest rates in Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru. Cases and deaths were projected to rise 30–50% by 2050 in most countries. Educational inequality was the most consistent determinant, associated with higher mortality overall and with both incidence and mortality among women, in whom the Human Development Index and H. pylori prevalence were also relevant.Conclusion. Educational inequality and H. pylori prevalence were most consistently associated with the gastric cancer burden, particularly among women.Policy Summary. Reducing the gastric cancer burden in Latin America will require policies that address educational inequality as a structural driver, alongside H. pylori screen-and-treat programs, dietary sodium reduction, and early detection in high-burden Andean countries.

title: 장기요양보험제도의 효과성 제고를 위한 연구 (Enhancing the Effectiveness of the Long-Term Care Insurance System)
affiliations: Korea Development Institute (KDI)

detail.title: 장기요양보험제도의 효과성 제고를 위한 연구 (Enhancing the Effectiveness of the Long-Term Care Insurance System)

publicationDetails.journalName: Korea Development Institute (KDI) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Korean Abstract: 
우리나라는 고령화의 진전에 따라 노인 의료비 지출이 증가하고 있으며, 특히 의료적 필요도는 낮지만 요양 필요도가 높은 노인이 고비용의 의료기관에 장기간 입원하는 이른바 사회적 입원 현상이 중요한 정책 과제로 지적되고 있다. 이러한 노인의 돌봄 수요 증가와 삶의 질 개선의 필요성, 그리고 비효율적인 의료비 지출 문제에 대응하기 위해 정부는 2008년에 노인장기요양보험제도를 도입하였다. 제도 도입 이후 장기요양 서비스의 대상과 범위는 지속적으로 확대되었으며, 도입 초기의 3등급 체계에서 경증 치매 노인을 포괄하는 6등급 체계로 개편되었다. 아울러 시설 중심의 급여 제공 방식에서 재가 중심으로 전환하고자 재가급여의 보장성도 강화되었다.

본 연구는 노인코호트 DB를 활용하여 노인장기요양보험제도가 의료비 지출에 미치는 대체 효과를 분석함으로써, 현행 노인장기요양보험제도의 효과성을 검토하고자 한다. 또한 이러한 결과를 토대로 향후 장기요양보험제도의 의료 이용 대체 효과를 제고할 수 있는 정책적 시사점을 제시한다. 실증분석 방법으로는 노인장기요양보험제도의 각 등급 기준점 근방에서 시설 및 재가 급여 비용이 외생적으로 변화한다는 점에 착안하여, 경사형 회귀불연속설계(Fuzzy Regression Disontinuity Design)와 사건사 분석(Event Study Design)을 활용하였다.
각 등급 기준점 근방의 신규 등급인정 신청자를 비교·분석한 결과, 중증도가 높은 1~2등급에서는 시설급여 또는 재가급여의 확대가 의료시설 이용과 의료비 지출을 감소시키는 것으로 나타났다. 병원 유형별로는 병원급 의료기관과 요양병원에서의 의료비 지출이 감소하였으며, 이용 형태별로는 입원비가 감소한 것으로 나타났다. 반면, 3~5등급에서는 재가급여의 확대가 의료시설 이용이나 의료비 지출을 감소시키는 효과가 관찰되지 않았다. 한편, 사건사 분석 결과, 경증 치매환자를 대상으로 하는 인지지원등급에서는 재가급여 확대가 의료비 지출을 감소시키는 효과가 확인되었다.


English Abstract: 
Korea’s rapid aging has brought the pressing policy concern of social hospitalization to the forefront. Older adults with low medical but high long-term care needs often occupy beds in high-cost medical institutions for extended periods―a trend that is driving up elderly medical spending. In 2008, the government introduced the Long-Term Care Insurance (LTCI) system to address the growing demand for care among older adults and improve their quality of life, while curbing inefficient medical spending. Since then, long-term care services have expanded in both eligibility and scope. The original three-grade classification was restructured into a six-grade system encompassing older adults with mild dementia, and home-based benefits were strengthened as part of a broader shift from facility-centered to home-centered care.

This study uses the Elderly Cohort Database of the National Health Insurance Service to examine how expanding LTCI affects medical expenditures. For identification, it employs a fuzzy regression discontinuity design and an event study design, exploiting the fact that LTCI grades are assigned based on the Long-Term Care Need Score and that the costs and benefits of these grade assignments shift exogenously around each threshold.

title: A Historical Lens on Modern Policy: The Evolution and Implementation of the Academic Bank of Credits in India
affiliations: , Regional Institute of Education, Bhubaneswar and Unaffiliated Author

detail.title: A Historical Lens on Modern Policy: The Evolution and Implementation of the Academic Bank of Credits in India
detail.abstract: This paper gives an overview of conceptual analysis of the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC), flagship policy of the government of India after the coming of NEP 2020. It asserts that ABC has the potential to shift the academia from a rigid institution centric framework to a more flexible learner directed framework where students can exercise the freedom of creating a personalized learning pathway which aligns with their unique traits. The ABC works on the digital ecosystem constituting of Digilocker, National Academic depository and APAAR ID. ABC will act as the "single verifiable source of truth" for academic archives which will remove the fear of losing documents, streamline academic process and make paperless administration a reality. The ABC has been compared with ECTS of Europe and U.S. Semester Credit Hours to get an idea of current practices across the world. The article also discusses the challenges in implementation of this ambitious project in a diverse and large nation like India which suffers from digital divide. The article concludes that ABC is a wonderful tool which can empower learners and the faculty in ensuring holistic development of learners in knowledge economy of the 21 st century.

title: Women's Status and the Struggle for Transformation: A Historical Review with Reference to Nepal
affiliations: Tribhuvan University, Sanothimi Campus

detail.title: Women's Status and the Struggle for Transformation: A Historical Review with Reference to Nepal
detail.abstract: Women's struggle for an honorable and respectable place in society dates back to antiquity. When the foundations of existing societies were laid, norms were established that placed women at the margins of society. This paper reviews the status of women in human society throughout history and examines its contemporary relevance. It reviews academic literature and selected historical and popular sources to gather information on the issue and identify women's struggle for emancipation. Employing a historical narrative review and a hermeneutic interpretive approach, the paper analyses women's status across different historical periods and societies, with particular reference to Nepal. It examines the position of Nepali women in comparison with the global feminist movement and evaluates the issues challenging their emancipation. It has shown that while Nepali women have gained progress at the legal and political level, the issues such as patriarchal norm, structural inequality as well as new patterns of digital and symbolic violence remain constraints toward the effective gender equality.

title: Liquidity Recovery and Market Hysteresis

detail.title: Liquidity Recovery and Market Hysteresis
detail.abstract: Electronic markets frequently rebuild visible depth after liquidity withdrawal, price displacement, or an episode of microstructural collapse. Yet the return of displayed quantity does not necessarily restore the market's capacity to absorb order flow, maintain stable queues, or withstand renewed stress. This paper develops a state-based theory of Liquidity Recovery and Market Hysteresis. It treats recovery as a multidimensional transition process rather than a visual judgment based on depth, spread, or price alone. The framework distinguishes displayed recovery, functional recovery, commitment recovery, structural recovery, price recovery, and broader state recovery, and it argues that these dimensions can proceed at different speeds, in different directions, and with different degrees of durability. Market hysteresis is defined as persistent dependence of post-disruption behavior on the path through which the market arrived at its current observable configuration. Under hysteresis, two order books with comparable price, spread, and displayed depth may possess materially different transition probabilities because their order-age distributions, queue composition, cancellation histories, replenishment mechanisms, latent-liquidity response, and commitment structure differ. The paper introduces a recovery vector, structural-distance measures, relaxation time, recovery quality, a hysteresis gap, and secondary-collapse risk. It also distinguishes rapid but fragile repair from slower, durable restoration. The theory integrates Liquidity Commitment Theory, Market State Dynamics, Liquidity Commitment Cascades, the Matching Engine Response Window, Event-Driven Microstructure Collapse, and Microstructural Pulse Dislocation. Its principal empirical prediction is that snapshot measures systematically overstate resilience during a material subset of post-disruption intervals. Markets with incomplete commitment and structural recovery should remain more susceptible to renewed withdrawal, wider spreads, elevated cancellation intensity, nonlinear price response, and secondary displacement even after visible depth appears normal. The paper develops falsifiable propositions and an empirical architecture suitable for exchange-sequenced market-by-order data, while preserving strict boundaries between observable state dynamics and claims about private intention, manipulation, or universal physical law. The proposed framework reframes resilience as the quality and persistence of restored market function, not merely the reappearance of liquidity.

title: Design-Phase Command Responsibility for Autonomous Cyber Weapons: Reorienting Article 28 of the Rome Statute to the Authorization Stage

detail.title: Design-Phase Command Responsibility for Autonomous Cyber Weapons: Reorienting Article 28 of the Rome Statute to the Authorization Stage

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None declared.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The work was conducted as part of doctoral research at the University of Cologne, Faculty of Law.

detail.abstract:
Abstract:

This article establishes a Design-Phase Command Responsibility doctrine for autonomous cyber weapons under Article 28 of the Rome Statute. The existing command responsibility framework presupposes that the commander exercises effective control over subordinates at the moment wrongful acts are committed. When autonomous cyber weapons eliminate contemporaneous human control at the targeting stage, this presupposition fails structurally — not because the law is inapplicable, but because the moment of legally relevant control has been relocated to the design and authorization phases that precede deployment by months or years. The article identifies three structural obstacles: the Black Box Problem (opacity prevents effective control at the engagement stage); the Temporal Displacement Problem (authorization precedes effects by intervals that defeat the "knew or had reason to know" standard); and the Causation Gap (automaticity of weapon execution severs the causal chain Article 28 presupposes). The article's principal doctrinal contribution is the Authorization-Stage Reorientation: Article 28 responsibility attaches at the moment a commander authorizes deployment of an autonomous system with knowledge — or reason to know — that its design-inherent opacity would foreseeably cause IHL violations. This reorientation is grounded in existing Article 28 jurisprudence from Hadžihasanović, Orić, and Bemba, extended to the authorization-stage context. The article further establishes that Article 25(3)(b) responsibility for ordering deployment of a Tier 3 system whose parameters foreseeably violate IHL constitutes an independent basis for individual criminal responsibility.

title:
Discrete Clusters Formulation through the Exploitation of Optimized K-modes Algorithm for Hypotheses Validation
in Social work Research: The Case of Greek Social Workers Working with Refugees
affiliations: , University of Patras, University of West Attica, University of West Attica and University of Miami - Miller School of Medicine

detail.title:
Discrete Clusters Formulation through the Exploitation of Optimized K-modes Algorithm for Hypotheses Validation
in Social work Research: The Case of Greek Social Workers Working with Refugees
detail.abstract: This article focuses on the results of self-funded quantitative research conducted by social workers working in the "refugee" crisis and social services in Greece (1). The research, among other findings, argues that front-line professionals possess specific characteristics regarding their working profile. Statistical methods in the research performed significance tests to validate the initial hypotheses concerning the correlation between dataset variables. On the contrary of this concept, in this work, we present an alternative approach for validating initial hypotheses through the exploitation of clustering algorithms. Toward that goal, we evaluated several frequently used clustering algorithms regarding their efficiency in feature selection processes, and we finally propose a modified k-Modes algorithm for efficient feature subset selection.

title: Counting Fills Misrepresents Liquidations: Evidence from a Complete On-Chain Derivatives Ledger

detail.title: Counting Fills Misrepresents Liquidations: Evidence from a Complete On-Chain Derivatives Ledger

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author operates perplog, a commercial orderflow analytics product for the Hyperliquid exchange, and trades on that venue. This constitutes a material interest in the venue whose public data this paper analyses, and it is declared rather than left to be discovered. No data from that product was used in this study: every figure derives from Hyperliquid's public requester-pays node-fills archive, reachable by anyone with an AWS account. A full statement, including the use of AI assistance under the author's direction, appears in the paper's Declarations section.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The study involves no human participants or patients; it analyses public market data. Published datasets replace on-chain account addresses with derived pseudonymous identifiers to avoid distributing a compiled map of accounts to losses.
declarations.funderStatement: None. This research received no external funding. Data access costs fell within AWS's free monthly egress allowance.

detail.abstract: Forced liquidations in cryptocurrency derivatives are almost always counted from exchange-published event feeds, in which one economic liquidation appears as several records. We quantify the resulting distortion on Hyperliquid, an on-chain perpetual-futures venue whose node-fills archive is complete and attributed to the liquidated account — a combination no centralised venue publishes. On a fixed-hour stratified sample of 351,540 liquidation episodes reconstructed from 2,010,042 fills over one year, counting fills rather than episodes inflates the event count by a factor of 5.72 (day-resampled 95% CI [5.47, 5.99]). The inflation is not a constant: it is size-dependent, rising from a median of 2 fills per episode below the median size to a median of 72 in the top percentile, so the bias is concentrated on precisely the events that liquidation studies are about. The top 1% of episodes generate 23.1% of all fills. We also characterise the episode-size distribution and report a negative result: the tail is unambiguously heavy — an exponential is rejected decisively — and it is not a power law, but it cannot be named beyond that. Lognormal and Weibull specifications both dominate a Pareto fit at every estimable threshold across nearly three orders of magnitude of cut-off, yet which of the two wins reverses with the threshold, so any named family would report the analyst's cut-off. Finally, the bias already documented in the literature runs the other way: rate-limited centralised-exchange feeds undercount, publishing per-second maxima rather than samples, while fill-level on-chain records overcount. Pooling the two sources combines a downward-biased count with an upward-biased one, and they do not cancel. All data, code and pre-registrations are public.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Scientific Research: Individual Benefits, Collective Risks, and a Framework for Responsible Research with AI
affiliations: University of Oslo - TIK-senteret, Maastricht University, University of East Anglia, SKEMA Business School, IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca, Scuola IMT Alti Studi Lucca, Luiss Guido Carli University - Department of Economics and Finance and University of Sussex - Science and Technology Policy Research Unit (SPRU)

detail.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Scientific Research: Individual Benefits, Collective Risks, and a Framework for Responsible Research with AI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the tension between the benefits of generative artificial intelligence (AI) for scientific research and the unresolved governance questions that accompany its rapid adoption. Drawing on an academic roundtable held at the AI for Science and Innovation Workshop (Scuola IMT Alti Studi Lucca, April 2026) and on a fast-expanding empirical literature, it maps the disagreement within the research community across four stages of the research process: funding, research tasks, publication and peer review, and use and uptake. The empirical case for AI's productivity, augmentation, and democratization effects has strengthened. The picture changes once productivity is disaggregated: AIassisted work shows measurable gains in publication volume and citation share, while the evidence on novelty, disruption, and breakthrough output remains ambiguous or negative. We argue that the divergence between private and social returns arises through three analytically distinct mechanisms, namely information asymmetry, negative externalities on a shared knowledge base, and depletion of research capacity, and that each calls for a different governance instrument. We propose Responsible Research with AI (RRAI), an extension of the Responsible Research and Innovation tradition organized around four principles that operate at different levels of the research system: disclosure, differentiation, narrative, and proportionality. RRAI builds on existing institutional scaffolding, including the EU AI Act, UNESCO, and the OECD, and aims to preserve AI's productivity gains while addressing systemic risks that individual researchers can neither observe nor manage on their own.

title: Caste and the Right to Learn: Policy, Practice, and Persistent Inequalities
affiliations: RIE (NCERT), Bhubaneswar, Utkal University Bhubaneswar, Odisha,  and Regional Institute of Education, Bhubaneswar

detail.title: Caste and the Right to Learn: Policy, Practice, and Persistent Inequalities
detail.abstract: This paper looks at the long-standing relationship between caste and the right to education in India, the paradox of progressive policies existing alongside deeply rooted inequalities. Though constitutional protections exist, affirmative action by reservation of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and Other Backward Classes (OBCs), and the groundbreaking Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, the article is a historical analysis of how ever-present disparities based on caste still influence educational experiences. The study is a critical analysis of on-the-ground realities, such as rural-urban disparities, gender-caste relationships, and structural determinants such as economic precarity, lack of social capital (Bourdieu), and neoliberal privatization based on empirical evidence in the form of sources such as ASER reports, AISHE data, and fieldwork studies. It ends with practical suggestions obtaining a better implementation of RTE, more reservations, caste-sensitivity training, Dalit-led movements and more action on the part of multiple stakeholders to bring education to its emancipatory potential, repeating the mantra of Ambedkar: Educate, Agitate, Organize.

title: Diversification of Portfolio Risk
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Diversification of Portfolio Risk
detail.abstract: This paper explains that phenomena like volatility clustering and volatility persistence that violate the assumptions of Modern Portfolio Theory become irrelevant in face of mathematical flaws in its computation of portfolio mean return and portfolio variance of returns. Empirical validation of the explanation is provided by studying the returns and variances of seven classes of assets in the US over the last 25 years and it is found that diversification of risk in a portfolio is not dependent on correlations between constituent asset returns but rather on the mean returnvariance ratio of the return series of the portfolio itself.

title: Inflation Hedging Potential of Different Classes of Assets
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Inflation Hedging Potential of Different Classes of Assets
detail.abstract: This paper studies the inflation hedging potential of four classes of assets-real estate, infrastructure, gold and stocks and finds that the extant mixed and inconclusive empirical evidence can be explained away with the help of regressions of levels instead of returns because regressions of levels are mathematically correct, while those of ratios (i.e. returns or rates) are not as they measure different economic phenomena. The levels regressions show that all the four asset markets grow with the economy providing partial hedging against inflation, with stocks providing nearly complete hedging as they are more finely adjusted to the economic environment.

title: Ethno-Science and Physics: Unveiling Historical Ingenuity for Modern Andragogy at Undergraduate Level in Odisha
affiliations: , Regional Institute of Education, Bhubaneswar, Department of Education, RIE, (NCERT) and Department of Education, RIE, (NCERT)

detail.title: Ethno-Science and Physics: Unveiling Historical Ingenuity for Modern Andragogy at Undergraduate Level in Odisha
detail.abstract: This article gives a theoretical scaffolding for changing history andragogy at the undergraduate level in Odisha by blending physics, history, and ethno-science. It investigates the possibilities of including emergent technologies in effective interdisciplinary teaching. The classroom should shift from passive memorization to active inquiry-based learning. The main argument is that Odisha’s cultural practices and tangible heritage are repositories of local wisdom which based on scientific principles which were aimed at the good of the community. Through in-depth case-studies of Konark sun temple, Puri Jagannath Temple, traditional weaving, ancient maritime heritage of Odisha, pottery, and traditional water conservation systems. This paper throws light on the implementation of principles of applied physics in the local wisdom of Odisha such as rotational mechanics, thermodynamics, fluid dynamics and acoustics. By using ethno-science to teach history students will easily form associations between their tangible cultural heritage and physics. The use of emergent technologies like virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), Mixed reality (MR) and Artificial intelligence (AI) is a catalyst for learning experiences that encourage critical thinking skills. This model is welcomed to do away with rote memorization as per the guidelines of NEP 2020. The paper concludes by mentioning suggestions for an interdisciplinary curriculum design.

title: Management of Portfolios
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Management of Portfolios
detail.abstract: This paper provides a mathematical explanation for the flaws in the formulae used for computing the mean and variance of the returns of the portfolios as given in the Modern Portfolio Theory of Markowitz (1952) and also for the inefficacy of conducting regression analyses of the portfolio returns with respect to the market portfolio as advocated by Jensen (1969). Consequently, we get increasing mean price for increased logical sophistication of the active management strategy for portfolios indicating that it is possible to pick up the winners in an efficient market if accepting the additional risk that accompanies such strategies.

title: Domestic Gas, Energy Security, and Regional Development: A Hybrid Top-Down/Bottom-Up General Equilibrium Assessment of Indonesia's North Hub Deepwater Gas Project
affiliations: Padjadjaran University - Faculty of Economics and Business

detail.title: Domestic Gas, Energy Security, and Regional Development: A Hybrid Top-Down/Bottom-Up General Equilibrium Assessment of Indonesia's North Hub Deepwater Gas Project

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Not available
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not available
declarations.funderStatement: Not available

detail.abstract: Indonesia's first ultra-deepwater gas development-the North Hub project in the Makassar Strait, about two billion cubic feet per day from two floating production, storage and offloading vessels (FP-SOs) at roughly US$3 billion each, with some 72% of the gas allocated to domestic use-poses a question a project cash-flow model cannot answer: what is such a project worth to the wider economy, and where do the gains accrue? I develop a hybrid topdown/bottom-up computable general equilibrium (CGE) model of Indonesia, derived explicitly from household and firm optimization and calibrated to a 2016 interregional input-output base. Gas delivery enters as competing activity-analysis technologies (FPSO versus pipeline) evaluated in general-equilibrium welfare terms; a dedicated fertilizer/petrochemical sector is derived so domestic gas reaches its true feedstock user; and an explicit 34-province topdown layer attributes production and fabrication to host regions. Modeled as a demand-growth expansion, North Hub keeps the domestic gas price broadly stable, raises household welfare by about 0.13%, expands the fertilizer/petrochemical sector by 7.9%, and lifts gross regional product in Kalimantan Timur by 6.6%, with a comparable construction-phase boost to Kepulauan Riau through FPSO fabrication. The national effect is modest but the strategic content is larger than the headline: the project reinforces the sector on which the widest span of the downstream economy depends.

title: Why the Future isn't Trading: Causally Inert Events as a Test for Time Travelers

detail.title: Why the Future isn't Trading: Causally Inert Events as a Test for Time Travelers
detail.abstract: We present a novel empirical argument against the existence of single-timeline backward time travel using the price behavior of prediction markets. If rational agents could travel backward in time, binary prediction contracts would collapse to degenerate prices-$1 or $0-from the moment of market inception. We observe no such behavior across hundreds of thousands of resolved contracts. This test is sharper than prior economic arguments (Reinganum, 1986) because it yields a directly falsifiable prediction, and more robust than physical experiments (Hawking, 1992) because it requires only the existence of a single profit-motivated agent anywhere in the future who is actually on a closed timelike curve intersecting the market's spacetime location. Crucially, rational time travelers would have no incentive to conceal trades on causally inert events (where outcomes are price-independent), making such arbitrage fundamentally unobservable in normal market activity yet glaringly obvious in aggregate price behavior. We acknowledge that many-worlds time travel evades our test. The only empirically testable model of backward time travel is the single-timeline model, and prediction markets appear to falsify it.

title: Labour Force Participation and Employment Dynamics in Haryana: A Comprehensive Analysis of PLFS Data (2017-18 to 2023-24)
affiliations: and Guru Jambheshwar University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Labour Force Participation and Employment Dynamics in Haryana: A Comprehensive Analysis of PLFS Data (2017-18 to 2023-24)
detail.abstract: This comprehensive academic report presents an in-depth analysis of Haryana's labour market dynamics utilizing Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) data from 2017-18 to 2023-24. The analysis covers seven consecutive years of labour force indicators and employment patterns, providing detailed insights into overall trends, gender dimensions, rural-urban disparities, sectoral composition, educational stratification, and youth employment challenges.

title: Connectedness in Motion: A Time-Varying Diebold-Yilmaz Framework in High Dimensions
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics and Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Connectedness in Motion: A Time-Varying Diebold-Yilmaz Framework in High Dimensions
detail.abstract: This paper develops a time-varying Diebold-Yilmaz framework for measuring connectedness in high-dimensional time series. The proposed framework combines the Diebold-Yilmaz connectedness measures with a high-dimensional time-varying vector autoregressive (VAR) model to characterize evolving connectedness networks. We first establish a sufficient condition for the local stationarity of high-dimensional time-varying VAR(p) processes and show the existence of a weakly dependent stationary approximation. Building on these results, we propose an easy-to-implement estimation procedure for time-varying generalized impulse response functions and connectedness measures, and derive uniform asymptotic error bounds for them in high dimensions. Extensive simulations demonstrate favorable finite-sample performance of the proposed method. An empirical study of volatility spillovers among global stock markets from 2005 to 2021 uncovers four pronounced cycles of systemic stress, a persistent core-periphery asymmetry in which North American and European markets transmit volatility shocks to Asia-Pacific markets, and two distinct crisis topologies, namely global contagion and regional containment, shaped by the degree of financial integration and institutional barriers.

title: Information, Institutions, and the Road: How Absent Common Knowledge Sustains the Peak-Hour Trap - and Why the State May Prefer It That Way
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Information, Institutions, and the Road: How Absent Common Knowledge Sustains the Peak-Hour Trap - and Why the State May Prefer It That Way

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest, financial or otherwise, in connection with the research presented in this paper. No funding was received for this work from any public, commercial, or not-for-profit funding body. The research was conducted independently, and the views expressed are solely those of the author.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.
declarations.funderStatement: This research does not involve human subjects, animal subjects, clinical trials, or the collection of personal data. Accordingly, ethics approval was not required for this study.

detail.abstract:
The companion papers establish that peak-hour urban congestion is a Bayes-Nash equilibrium sustained by a self-confirming homogeneous prior (Deep, 2026a), and that it constitutes a Tragedy of the Commons in temporal road capacity solvable by institutional information provision (Deep, 2026b). The present paper asks the prior question: why does the institutional information failure persist? If road state information is available at near-zero marginal cost and its provision would dissolve the congestion equilibrium, why does the state not provide it?
We answer by modelling the state as a strategic player in the congestion game alongside commuters. The state collects fiscal revenue proportional to vehicle use: fuel excise duties, motor vehicle taxes, and tolls. We establish empirically that this revenue is scally significant- exceeding Rs. 7.5 lakh crore annually across Indian central and state governments, with fuel taxes constituting approximately 18.4% of Central gross tax revenues and road transport taxes constituting ap proximately 4.3% of state own-tax revenues. We formalise this as a state moral hazard: the state’s payo is a weighted sum of social welfare and fiscal revenue, and the fiscal revenue component is increasing in congestion. When the fiscal revenue weight βS exceeds a critical threshold β∗ S, the state’s individually optimal action is to withhold road-state information, sustaining the homogeneous prior µH and the simultaneous-departure equilibrium that generates congestion and therefore fuel consumption and tax revenue.

title: Geoeconomic Fragmentation, Security Exceptions, and the Weaponisation of Economic Interdependence in International Economic Law

detail.title: Geoeconomic Fragmentation, Security Exceptions, and the Weaponisation of Economic Interdependence in International Economic Law
detail.abstract: The contemporary international economic order is undergoing a policy-driven reversal of globalization as States increasingly deploy trade, investment, financial, and technological instruments as tools of strategic coercion. This paper examines the legal, institutional, and economic dimensions of this reversal, with particular focus on the invocation of national security exceptions, most notably GATT Article XXI, and the 'weaponization' of economic interdependence through tariffs, export controls, financial sanctions, investment screening mechanisms, and critical mineral restrictions. It analyses the conceptual framework of weaponized interdependence, the structure and evolution of security exceptions across international economic law instruments, and landmark jurisprudence that has established, and simultaneously revealed the fragility of, multilateral constraints on security exception abuse. The paper examines the specific mechanisms through which economic interdependence has been weaponized, and assesses the quantitative and qualitative economic consequences of fragmentation, with particular attention to the disproportionate burden borne by developing and emerging market economies. The paper argues that the tension between legitimate security imperatives and systemic welfare costs is resolvable only through interpretive clarification of security exception thresholds, plurilateral disciplines on weaponized instruments, restoration of functioning appellate dispute settlement, and protective mechanisms for non-aligned and developing States. The paper concludes that the current trajectory of unchecked fragmentation threatens the structural foundations of international stability, and that the hard lessons of interwar economic nationalism remain as relevant as ever to the choices confronting States and negotiators today.

title:
Point-In-Time Data Integrity in Quantitative Equity Research 

A Reproducible Framework for Eliminating Look-Ahead Bias

detail.title:
Point-In-Time Data Integrity in Quantitative Equity Research 

A Reproducible Framework for Eliminating Look-Ahead Bias
detail.abstract: Financial statements describe economic periods, but quantitative researchers can trade on their contents only after those contents become public and operationally usable. When a database associates a financial fact with its fiscal period end, overwrites the historical record with a later revision, or ignores the timing of an earnings release relative to the market session, a backtest may use information that investors did not possess. This paper develops a reproducible framework for controlling that class of look-ahead bias. The framework separates fiscal valid time from public, system and tradable time; stores financial facts in a bitemporal model; preserves original and restated disclosures; classifies single-quarter, year-to-date and annual durations; derives fourth-quarter observations with explicit parent lineage; and records each transformation in a cryptographically identifiable experiment manifest. A controlled empirical design compares four information sets: period-end/latest-value, filing-date/latest-value, acceptance-time/original-value and tradable-time/original-value. All other factor, portfolio, risk and cost assumptions are held fixed. The paper also reports a pilot implementation using a limited U.S. large-cap sample from 2018–2024. The pilot is not treated as a population estimate of point-in-time distortion; it demonstrates the downstream research pipeline and shows that a value composite remained positive under sector neutralization and progressively conservative transaction and borrow-cost assumptions, while several alternative factor candidates did not survive the same validation sequence. In a bounded version of the controlled experiment on 342 large-cap U.S. stocks over 2018–2024, activating facts at the fiscal period end with later-revised values (Version A) inflated measured CAPM alpha for every factor tested relative to a strict tradable point-in-time set (Version D), significantly so for the most timing-sensitive families, earnings surprise and accruals; a full-market estimate is left for future work. The principal contribution is methodological: a backtest should be described as point-in-time only when every input can be shown to have been observable, admissible and executable at the moment the strategy used it.

title: Optimal Systemic Risk Management
affiliations: , Grenoble Ecole de Management and

detail.title: Optimal Systemic Risk Management
detail.abstract: We study the maximization of a law-invariant multivariate functional over the Fréchet class of joint distributions with fixed marginals, subject to a budget constraint. To solve the problem, we propose a stochastic swapping algorithm that enforces cost-efficiency at every step while allowing for objectives that are not necessarily convex functions of the aggregate sum. We show that, depending on the level of the budget constraint, the optimal solution exhibits a dependence structure ranging from strong positive dependence to strong negative dependence.

title: The Rise of the Skills Agenda in African Education Reforms, 1970-2021

detail.title: The Rise of the Skills Agenda in African Education Reforms, 1970-2021
detail.abstract: This study examines the evolution of the skills agenda in education reform across 52 African countries between 1970 and 2021. Employing rule-based deductive computational discourse analysis, it classifies 3,219 education reforms within a two-dimensional framework that distinguishes skills focus (foundational and cognitive, technical and vocational, science and technology, socio-emotional, and entrepreneurial skills) from development mechanism (access expansion, curriculum reform, governance and qualifications, and labor market linkage). Skills-oriented reforms account for 30.5% of all education reforms and increased steadily over time, with the odds of a reform prioritizing skills rising by 3.4% annually, corresponding to a 5.4-fold increase across the study period. Foundational and cognitive skills and technical and vocational skills dominated throughout, while governance and qualifications remained uncommon despite a recent rise in labor market linkage. The study provides a longitudinal account of policy commitment to skills development, extending institutional analyses of education reform through a continent-wide perspective.

title: Fission and Finance: Preparing India's Insolvency Law for the Nuclear Age
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Fission and Finance: Preparing India's Insolvency Law for the Nuclear Age
detail.abstract: India intends to increase its nuclear energy capacity from 8.8 GW today to 100 GW by 2047; as a prelude, the sector has been opened to private players. Stretch targets enable quantum leaps in an enabling environment, but casualties along the wayside are inevitable. The nuclear industry is especially prone to this phenomenon, with a consistent track record of distress and insolvency following the euphoric boom of every past nuclear cycle. This paper examines a number of such insolvencies in detail, including those of the Washington Public Power Supply System, British Energy Plc, Westinghouse Electric Corporation, and USEC Inc., with several other cases referenced in brief. An additional characteristic of the industry is that it operates predominantly under government ownership, which not only ensures the primacy of national interest but also shields companies from the risk of formal insolvency. Areva and EDF in France, both of which had private sector participation, were rescued by the French government and have since been returned to state control. In the United States, the freest of markets, with several private sector players, increasing government intervention is evident, including equity stakes and preferential fuel supply arrangements, as the country seeks to leapfrog the competition. Delayed project execution has been the norm in India, across both nuclear and other infrastructure projects. The average construction time for a nuclear plant exceeds ten years; delivering 90 GW of additional capacity in twenty years will therefore almost certainly result in a number of insolvencies along the way. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 is not adequately equipped to deal with the nuances that will arise in such proceedings, a surefire recipe for litigation, which has plagued the Code since its inception. This paper brings to the fore the core issues that policymakers and practitioners will encounter. A reasoned deliberation on these matters can yield solutions that will strengthen the Code well before India confronts its first nuclear insolvency.

title: AI Adoption and Skill Demand
affiliations: , University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School and University of Pennsylvania - Management Department

detail.title: AI Adoption and Skill Demand

declarations.funderStatement: The authors thank the Mack Institute for generous funding support.

detail.abstract: Technological change redistributes the division of labor between people and capital and thus changes the skills firms seek from their employees. In this research, we ask how the adoption of AI technologies changes jobs. We suggest that AI adoption may automate discrete and codifiable tasks, placing more emphasis on novel or ill-defined problems and intra-organizational coordination. Accordingly, we examine whether AI adoption is associated with greater demand for complex problem solving skills, process-and communication-oriented skills, and experience and breadth through which such skills are built. Using rich data on approximately 164 million job postings in the United States from January 2021 to March 2026, we find that firm-level AI adoption is associated with increased demand in problem-solving skills, process skills, and social skills, as well as increased demand for experience and skill breadth. We show that it is not just the result of changes in the composition of demand across occupations but instead reflects a reconfiguration of skills within roles. Our results highlight how technological change changes the bundle of skills firms seek even when they continue hiring for the same role and provide insights for workers seeking to understand what skills retain value following the emergence of novel generative AI technologies.

title: MARLEY: A waste-free autonomous observatory for long-term monitoring of cold-water coral health and behaviour
affiliations: Ifremer, Ifremer, Ifremer, Ifremer, Ifremer and IFREMER

detail.title: MARLEY: A waste-free autonomous observatory for long-term monitoring of cold-water coral health and behaviour
detail.abstract: Cold-water coral reefs, classified as vulnerable marine ecosystems, and as such, their good conservation status is a target for an increasing number of regional and international regulations. Beyond present-day anthropogenic disturbances, deep-sea corals are under long-term threat from ocean warming and acidification. These ecosystem changes call for the implementation of long-term and high frequency ocean monitoring systems.,Here we present the design, implementation, and operational performance of the MARLEY observatory (Monitoring deep-seA coRaL EcosYstems), an autonomous, multi-parameter platform deployed in the Lampaul Canyon (Bay of Biscay) at 776 metres depth to monitor cold-water coral health with minimal environmental footprint. A primary design objective was to eliminate the deposition of dead weight on the seafloor, which represents a significant source of cumulative waste. To achieve this, MARLEY incorporates reversible ballasts enabling dynamic buoyancy adjustment during deployment and recovery. The platform features a decoupled camera module that allows flexible positioning of sensors relative to coral colonies while maintaining the main lander on sedimented peripheries.,For its first deployment in the Lampaul Canyon (Bay of Biscay), MARLEY successfully monitored Madrepora oculata polyp behaviour, associated fauna, and environmental parameters over a five-month operational period. Video data processing employed convolutional neural networks to classify polyp behaviour. Associated fauna was annotated via the Ocean Spy citizen science platform, demonstrating effective public engagement. Despite current limitations in real-time automated analysis, MARLEY demonstrates the feasibility of long-term, waste-free deep-sea observatories capable of generating essential variables for coral ecosystem health assessment and conservation management.

title: From Skeletons to Brains: Artificial Intelligence, Mineral Intensity of Use (MIOU), and Critical Mineral Intensity of Use (CMIOU) in an Endogenous Growth Framework

detail.title: From Skeletons to Brains: Artificial Intelligence, Mineral Intensity of Use (MIOU), and Critical Mineral Intensity of Use (CMIOU) in an Endogenous Growth Framework

declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded

detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether the diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) and AIintensive digital capital alters the composition-rather than merely the level-of mineral demand. Drawing on the mineral intensity of use literature, endogenous growth theory, and recent research on critical minerals, we argue that AI induces a structural transition from bulk industrial minerals ("skeleton minerals") toward critical digital-energy minerals ("brain minerals"). We formalize this distinction through two complementary intensity measures: Mineral Intensity of Use (MIOU), which captures the economywide consumption of bulk skeleton minerals per unit of output, and Critical Mineral Intensity of Use (CMIOU), which captures the consumption of critical brain minerals per unit of output. Using a balanced country-year panel covering sixteen economies over 2005-2025, we estimate two-way fixed-effects and difference-indifferences specifications with a calibrated empirical dataset. The results indicate that post-2015 AI exposure is associated with a statistically significant decline in MIOU and a commensurate rise in CMIOU, with a widening divergence between the two. The evidence supports what we term the structural inversion hypothesis: AI does not simply dematerialize production but reorganizes its mineral foundations-compressing MIOU while expanding CMIOU. We discuss implications for industrial policy, mineral security, and downstream industrial development in resource-endowed economies, and we outline a roadmap for future estimation using observed mineral consumption, semiconductor trade, and datacenter capacity data.

title: Expected Credit Loss Framework -Implications on Profitability and Viability of Indian Banks

detail.abstract: India's banking sector has long operated under an incurred loss provisioning regime, recognising credit losses only upon observable evidence of default-a design that systematically delays loss recognition and encourages the accumulation of unacknowledged risk. In response, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued a Discussion Paper on Introduction of the Expected Credit Loss (ECL) Framework for Provisioning by Banks in January 2023, followed by Draft Directions on Asset Classification, Provisioning and Income Recognition in October 2025, with implementation targeted from 1 April 2027. This paper investigates how the transition to forward-looking ECL provisioning is likely to affect the profitability and financial viability of Indian scheduled commercial banks. Because the framework is not yet in force, the Provisions-to-Gross Advances Ratio is used as a theoretically grounded proxy for ECL recognition intensity-a substitution justified both by the structural equivalence between IRACP and ECL mechanics, and by the RBI's explicit anchoring of ECL prudential floors to existing IRACP rates. Using a panel of 587 bank-year observations drawn from the RBI Database on Indian Economy (DBIE) over 2016-2023, a pooled OLS model is estimated with Net Profit Ratio as the dependent variable and Gross NPA Ratio and CRAR as controls. The results reveal a statistically significant positive association between provisioning intensity and profitability (β = 1.243, p < 0.001), while asset quality deterioration is robustly negative (β =-0.0052, p < 0.001) and capital adequacy is positively linked to earnings (β = 0.0071, p = 0.044). The model accounts for 88.9% of profitability variation (R² = 0.889). These findings carry a clear implication: banks that enter the ECL era with stronger balance sheets and disciplined provisioning practices are well-placed to absorb the transition, while those burdened by legacy NPAs and thin capital buffers face a materially harder path. The paper makes an original empirical contribution to the emerging Indian ECL readiness literature and offers actionable pre-implementation insights for regulators, bank boards, and investors.

title: The Relevance of Catholic Social thought for Law
affiliations: Seattle University School of Law

detail.title: The Relevance of Catholic Social thought for Law
detail.abstract: I have been explicit in some of my scholarship in considering principles, methods and insights from the tradition of Catholic Social Thought, but, more often than not, the consideration is implicit, serving as the motivation for addressing particular research questions. There are a variety of ways to consider Catholic social teaching and its implications for law. Scholars have identified various core principles rooted in scriptures and the teaching of the Church. Many summaries begin with the Papal Encyclical Rerum Novarum (On the Rights and Duties of Capital and Labor) issued by Pope Leo XIII in 1891.2 I will get there eventually, but I want to begin with a method that is deeply embedded in Catholic Social Thought and gives it the potential to be more generalizable outside of explicitly Catholic or Christian contexts.

title: Non-Asymptotic Stability and Turnover of Risk-Parity Allocations: ERC Smoothness and Hierarchical Boundary Effects

detail.title: Non-Asymptotic Stability and Turnover of Risk-Parity Allocations: ERC Smoothness and Hierarchical Boundary Effects

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no financial, personal, professional, or institutional relationships that could have influenced, or could reasonably be perceived to have influenced, the research presented in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is theoretical and methodological, uses no human participants, patient data, personal data, animal subjects, interviews, surveys, or experimental interventions requiring ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently within Alpha Stochastic Research.

detail.abstract: We study the sensitivity of two long-only covariance-based allocation rules: Equal Risk Contribution (ERC) and a precisely specified single-linkage, tree-recursive hierarchical allocator using equal-weight cluster variances, which we denote by EW-HRP. The distinction between a fixed tree and an estimated tree is central. First, the normalized ERC map is shown to be C∞ on the cone of positive-definite covariance matrices and uniformly Lipschitz on every spectral set {Σ : Σ ⪰ λI}, with the explicit bound ∥wERC(Σ1) − wERC(Σ0)∥2 ≤ 2 √ N λ ∥Σ1 − Σ0∥F . Second, for every fixed binary tree T , the corresponding hierarchical allocation map is smooth. On Kλ,Λ := {Σ : λI ⪯ Σ ⪯ ΛI}, its derivative is bounded explicitly in terms of the tree depth. Third, the estimated-tree allocation is locally smooth away from distance ties but can be discontinuous at topology boundaries. We give an exact three-asset example in which the one-sided portfolio limits differ by 38/71 in ℓ1 norm, and a second exact example showing that no strictly positive jump can hold uniformly over all topology boundaries. Finally, for ridge-regularized rolling covariance matrices and bounded independent returns, we derive deterministic and expected finite-sample turnover bounds. The smooth component scales as √ n/T in expectation for two windows separated by n observations, while topology changes contribute an additional term bounded by their crossing probability. The results isolate boundary crossings as a distinct turnover mechanism without asserting a universal ordering between ERC and hierarchical allocations.

title: Media Attention Structural Inequality: A Comparative Analysis of Parasport and Traditional Sport Coverage

detail.title: Media Attention Structural Inequality: A Comparative Analysis of Parasport and Traditional Sport Coverage
detail.abstract: This study presents a systematic empirical investigation of structural inequality in the media representation of adaptive (Paralympic) sport relative to conventional sport across Russia's two dominant digital sports platforms, Championat.com and Sports.ru. Employing a concurrent mixed-methods research design that integrates quantitative content analysis of website and social media output with a sociological survey instrument administered to 290 respondents, the research generates precise, triangulated measurements of the informational asymmetry between these two categories of sport coverage. Findings reveal a publication ratio of 528:0.07 (Championat.com) and 80:0 (Sports.ru) in average daily terms during non-Paralympic periods, providing full empirical confirmation of both the structural inequality hypothesis (H₁) and the audience perception hypothesis (H₂). Theoretical interpretation proceeds through the analytical frameworks of agenda-setting theory, framing theory, cultural hegemony, the social construction of reality, and Bourdieuian symbolic inequality. The study makes an original contribution to the underexplored intersection of disability media studies and Russian sports journalism scholarship, offering a replicable methodological framework and a set of evidence-based recommendations addressed to editorial boards, sports governing bodies, and relevant state authorities.

title: Debt Recovery and Bank Performance in Nigeria: Evidence from Panel Data Analysis
affiliations: University of Calabar- Department of Banking & Finance, University of Calabar, University of Calabar, Calabar Nigeria and University of Calabar, Calabar Nigeria

detail.title: Debt Recovery and Bank Performance in Nigeria: Evidence from Panel Data Analysis
detail.abstract: High non-performing loan levels continue to threaten the profitability and stability of Nigerian banks, yet the empirical link between debt recovery practices and bank performance over an extended period remains underexplored. Anchored in credit rationing theory of Stiglitz and Weiss and the psychological theory of credit recovery, the study used panel data from seven Nigerian banks (2004-2023, 140 observations). Four credit recovery indicators, NPL ratio, loan loss provisions, debt recovery rate, and write-off ratio-were regressed against net income and ROE using a Random Effects panel model, selected via Hausman and unit root tests. Loan recoveries (β = 0.106, p = 0.047), write-offs (β = 0.145, p = 0.002), and loan loss provisions (β = 0.419, p = 0.000) all had significant positive effects on net income, with the model explaining 42.7% of the variation (R² = 0.4272). it concludes that credit recovery, write-offs, and provisioning practices significantly enhance Nigerian bank performance, confirming that credit risk management is a key driver of profitability rather than a mere compliance exercise. The study offers rare two-decade panel evidence jointly assessing recoveries, write-offs, and provisioning in Nigerian banking, provides empirical support for credit rationing theory in an African context, and reveals a strategic role for write-offs in balance-sheet management, an area prior studies have largely overlooked.it is recommended that Nigerian banks should strengthen proactive loan recovery mechanisms, such as enhanced credit monitoring systems, dedicated recovery units, and data analytics for tracking delinquent loans, while adopting transparent, strategic write-off policies and maintaining forward-looking, IFRS 9aligned provisioning standards to sustain profitability and manage credit risk effectively.

title:
Beyond Unemployment: Measuring Graduate Labour Underutilization in Nigeria 
Informality and Occupational Mismatch Among Nigeria's Tertiary-Educated Workforce

detail.title:
Beyond Unemployment: Measuring Graduate Labour Underutilization in Nigeria 
Informality and Occupational Mismatch Among Nigeria's Tertiary-Educated Workforce

declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is based exclusively on anonymized secondary survey data from the Nigeria Labour Force Survey.

detail.abstract: Across much of the developing world, headline unemployment is a poor measure of how well the labour market serves its most educated workers. Nigeria illustrates the problem starkly. Official statistics report modest unemployment among the tertiary-educated: 9.0 percent for postsecondary and 2.0 percent for postgraduate holders in the first quarter of 2024. Two decades of Nigerian scholarship have nonetheless described graduate unemployment and underemployment as a national crisis. This paper argues that the two accounts are not in conflict once graduate labour underutilization, defined jointly through informality, occupational skill mismatch, and time-related underemployment, is measured directly rather than inferred from the unemployment rate. Using individual-level microdata from all six quarters of the Nigeria Labour Force Survey currently available, the first quarter of 2024 through the second quarter of 2025, we construct and validate these three indicators against official benchmarks, estimate their association with education tier net of demographic and geographic composition, and decompose overall underutilization into the share attributable to each condition. Composite informality and occupational mismatch both decline sharply and significantly with education tier, a relationship that survives controls for age, sex, urban or rural residence, state, and quarter. Time-related underemployment shows no significant tier gradient once the same controls are applied, indicating that its raw association with education level in the descriptive data reflects demographic and geographic composition rather than a genuine effect of credential level. A Shapley decomposition shows that informality accounts for roughly half of overall graduate underutilization at every education tier, with occupational mismatch accounting for most of the remainder and time-related underemployment a consistently minor contributor. Even among postgraduate degree holders, more than a quarter remain informally employed and roughly a quarter remain occupationally mismatched, at a point in the education distribution where headline unemployment is close to zero. This paper is the first in a planned sequence: it establishes the measurement and documents the pattern; a second paper will examine how employment quality mediates the wage returns to tertiary education, and a third will test competing theoretical accounts of why mismatch and informality persist using richer, cohortaware modelling.

title: The Algorithm as Congestion: Navigation Systems, Information Homogenisation, and the Self-Defeating Forecast
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Algorithm as Congestion: Navigation Systems, Information Homogenisation, and the Self-Defeating Forecast

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest, financial or otherwise, in connection with the research presented in this paper. No funding was received for this work from any public, commercial, or not-for-profit funding body. The research was conducted independently, and the views expressed are solely those of the author.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research does not involve human subjects, animal subjects, clinical trials, or the collection of personal data. Accordingly, ethics approval was not required for this study.

detail.abstract: The standard economic account of information holds that providing agents with better information moves equilibrium outcomes closer to the social optimum. Centralised navigation algorithms appear to instantiate this logic, yet urban congestion has worsened in precisely the cities where algorithmic routing penetration is highest. This paper identities two structural design failures that explain this paradox. The first is information homogenisation: broadcasting a common routing signal causes rational agents to discard heterogeneous private local knowledge, collapsing the natural route diversity that had functioned as a decentralised co ordination mechanism approximating the social optimum. The second is the self defeating forecast: any estimated time of arrival computed from current traffic conditions without internalising the algorithm’s own routing effect is structurally downward biased, with bias increasing in the number of simultaneous users and the congestion sensitivity of the recommended route- a form of the Lucas (1976) critique applied to navigation systems. We prove that these two failures com pound- the Compounded Ineficiency Theorem- to produce an equilibrium that can be welfare-inferior to the no-information benchmark of Part III, under conditions empirically plausible for major urban corridors. The key prior result in this area, Acemoglu et al.’s (2018) Informational Braess Paradox, shows that more information can harm welfare in routing games. We extend this finding by identifying the precise mechanism- algorithm design failure rather than information provision per se- and by characterising a truth-telling algorithm that corrects both failures through internalised ETA formation and stochastic route diversification, achieving the social optimum in expectation. Empirical grounding is provided by Cabannes et al. (2019) on the I-210 corridor, Bagabaldo et al. (2024) on optimal partial adoption, and Monnot et al. (2017) on the empirical Price of Anarchy in Singapore.

title: Challenges in Implementing ICAO TRAINAIR PLUS Standards in National Aviation Training Institutions: The Case of DHMI Türkiye

detail.title: Challenges in Implementing ICAO TRAINAIR PLUS Standards in National Aviation Training Institutions: The Case of DHMI Türkiye
detail.abstract: Implementing ICAO's TRAINAIR PLUS standards in national aviation training institutions demands significant organizational, regulatory, and capacity-building efforts. This study examines the case of Türkiye's State Airports Authority (DHMİ) as it works to align its Aviation Academy with TRAINAIR PLUS. Using a qualitative case study approach, we analyze DHMİ directives, ICAO documents, and academic literature to identify key challenges-such as regulatory restructuring, adopting competency-based training, developing STPs, enhancing instructor capacity, and integrating e-learning. Comparative examples from South Korea, Thailand, and Ukraine show these challenges are globally shared. The study also explores opportunities like international recognition, course sharing, and revenue generation. We conclude with strategic recommendations for DHMİ and similar institutions to strengthen ICAO alignment through improved management support, instructor development, and quality assurance.

detail.abstract:
The Internal Rate of Return has long served as the anchor metric for evaluating private equity
performance, yet this near-universal adoption conceals a signicant algebraic fragility. This paper
examines IRR's embedded bias arising from subscription-line-of-credit distortion, cash ow timing
sensitivity, and the risk of multiple solutions within its polynomial function. Using an axiomatic
approach, it analyzes the scale-insensitivity anomaly, examining how performance metrics respond
to changes in capital scale.
The central nding formally demonstrates that blindness to capital scale is not a defect unique
to IRR, but a mathematical property inherent to ratio-based metrics as a category  including
the Kaplan-Schoar Public Market Equivalent (KS-PME). The implication is signicant: pursuing
an impressive return percentage without measuring real capital-absorption capacity can undermine
portfolio eciency for large institutional limited partners.
As a policy recommendation, this paper proposes an industry reporting standard that pairs KS-
PME as a benchmark for external alpha quality with TVPI/DPI as the anchor for absolute dollar
scale. The goal is a reporting standard that is more transparent and accountable to the limited
partners whose capital the industry manages.

title: Towards a Sustainable Future: The Impact of Green Finance, Governance, and Digitalization on Global Emissions

detail.title: Towards a Sustainable Future: The Impact of Green Finance, Governance, and Digitalization on Global Emissions

detail.abstract: This research empirically investigates the macroeconomic factors that are driving carbon dioxide (CO2) emission among the top 30 emitting nations (2000-2021). This study uses an augmented STIRPAT framework employing a second-generation Autoregressive Distributed Lag using Pooled Mean Group estimator (PMG-ARDL) model, further cross validated using FMOLS and DOLS estimators. This research simultaneously evaluates green finance, institutional governance, technological innovation and digitalization. The findings confirm the Environmental Kuznets Curve's technique effect, as green finance significantly reduces longrun emissions. However, this study unveils a critical "institutional governance paradox", demonstrating that strong governance structures currently prioritize carbon-intensive economic expansion over ecological constraints. Furthermore, the analysis also quantifies a "digital rebound effect" and the macroeconomic Jevons Paradox, which proves that generalized technological innovation and digital innovation expansion actively increase absolute emissions. To achieve global carbon neutrality requires abandoning the growth-first paradigm, enforcing strict environmental policy stringency, and decoupling the digital economy from fossil fuel dependent grids.

title: From Newman to Salman: Informed Trading Penalties and Management Disclosure
affiliations: University of Michigan, Stephen M. Ross School of Business and University of Michigan, Stephen M. Ross School of Business

detail.title: From Newman to Salman: Informed Trading Penalties and Management Disclosure
detail.abstract: When prices are noisy, the presence of a few informed investors can cause other investors to demand additional costly disclosures from management. However, it is difficult to empirically identify informed traders' information advantage. This paper exploits the Second Circuit's decision in United States v. Newman (2014), which raised the evidentiary standard for prosecuting certain forms of insider trading by outside investors and increased their ability to trade on material, nonpublic information. This ruling is thus a shock that increased informed traders' trading ability while leaving uninformed traders' information sets unchanged. Post-ruling increases in managerial disclosures can then be attributed to uninformed investor concerns about the increased ability of informed traders to exploit their information advantage. We find that firms subject to Newman significantly increase voluntary public disclosure, particularly management earnings guidance and firm-initiated press releases, by 13% compared to control firms not subject to Newman. These effects reverse when Newman was reversed by the Supreme Court in Salman v. United States (2016). The disclosure effects are stronger in firms with both hedge funds, our proxy for informed investors, and non-hedge fund institutional investors, who are likely both concerned about being at an information disadvantage relative to hedge funds and also have influence over management. These results are also stronger when disclosure is a salient governance practice for the firm's nonhedge fund institutional investors, i.e., when they have other disclosing firms in their portfolio. Finally, the disclosure effects are also stronger when CEOs have higher pre-period stock pricebased incentives, consistent with the idea that investors employ both direct and incentive-based governance practices to induce management to make costly voluntary disclosures.

title: Managerial Tax Attention and Corporate Tax Outcomes

detail.abstract: We construct a measure of corporate tax attention from the text of quarterly earnings calls for U.S. public firms over 2007 to 2023 using an unsupervised topic model. The measure captures within-firm deviations in the attention corporate executives pay to tax related issues from the firm's own historical same-quarter baseline. We find that elevated tax attention predicts lower cash effective tax rates over horizons of up to three years and generates positive announcement returns. A triple difference-indifferences design exploiting the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 shows that firms with high pre-reform tax attention and high effective tax rates captured the largest post-reform reductions in effective tax rates. Analysts revise earnings forecasts upward and realized earnings subsequently exceed their revised forecasts, consistent with partial incorporation of a signal that is available but costly to extract.

title: Inferring the Political Weights of Presidential Candidates from Their Tax Policy Proposals
affiliations: and  University of Wisconsin

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
